confirmed.title: Retry loop ignores the caller's abort; an already-aborted attempt leaves an unhandled rejection
confirmed.defect: The attempt loop never checks `signal.aborted`. The module header and the code comment promise that no attempt starts after the caller's abort fires, but only the entry checks enforce it. If the signal fires during the backoff sleep, the next iteration still calls `call.transport.send(...)`. `untilAborted` then sees `signal.aborted` and does `return onAbort()`. That rejects the wrapper, but it never attaches a handler to `run`, the promise `send` just returned. When `send` rejects, nothing handles it.
confirmed.failureScenario: A Jev caller that passes a signal and keeps the default retry gets a 429 or 529. Examples are `lib/coach/role-advice.ts`, `lib/server/taste-chips.ts` and `lib/log/sanity.ts`. The request is cancelled or the turn deadline fires during the 400 ms backoff. The second attempt still starts and `postSystemOne` calls `fetch` with an already-aborted combined signal. That `fetch` rejects with an AbortError nobody handles. Under Node's default `--unhandled-rejections=throw` this is an unhandledRejection event that can crash the function or fail the request. It also bills nothing but consumes `beforeRetry` budget (in callers that meter retries) and a Jev request-budget slot.
confirmed.evidence: lib/ai/call.ts:128-131 (loop top checks only the deadline and `beforeRetry`); :135-136 `call.transport.send(...)` is invoked inside `untilAborted(...)`; :86-93 `untilAborted` returns `onAbort()` when `signal.aborted` without `run.catch`. The only abort checks are at lib/ai/call.ts:187 and :213 (entry and post-reserve).
votes: confirmed: I read the code and the defect is real, but its impact is smaller than "medium" suggests. The attempt loop in lib/ai/call.ts (about lines 268-292) checks only the deadline and beforeRetry. It never checks signal.aborted. The documented rule that no attempt starts after the caller's abort holds only at the entry checks (lines 187 and 213). Jev's retry policy (lib/ai/typesafe.ts:229) retries only on ProviderHttpError with a status in RETRYABLE_STATUSES (429/529, per the finding), and passes options.signal through. So a signal that fires during the 400 ms backoff reaches the next iteration, which calls call.transport.send(AbortSignal.any([deadline, signal])). postSystemOne then calls fetch with an already-aborted signal, and that fetch rejects with AbortError. untilAborted (lines 86-93) sees signal.aborted and runs `return onAbort()` before it attaches `run.then(...)`. The promise send returned therefore has no handler, so its rejection is unhandled. I did not run it; this is from reading the code, and call.test.ts has no abort-during-backoff case. The same path also wastes a Jev request-budget slot and a beforeRetry slot (in callers that meter retries) on a call nobody is waiting for. The caller still gets an AbortError, and Jev callers degrade to null, so the user-visible result is unchanged. Whether the unhandled rejection crashes the process depends on the runtime's unhandledRejection handling. Next.js and Vercel normally log it rather than exit, which makes "can crash the function" unlikely. I found no guard upstream and no owner ruling that accepts this. I rate it low, not medium. Fix: check signal.aborted at the top of each loop iteration and break, and have untilAborted attach `run.catch(() => {})` before the early return.

confirmed: I reproduced it with a vitest snippet on the real callModel. The snippet used a mocked call registry, a transport whose first send throws a 429, and a sleep hook that aborts the caller's signal during the backoff. The second send was still called, so two sends ran. The rejection from that second send was unhandled, and the process saw one unhandledRejection event. Code path: attempt() in lib/ai/call.ts has no signal.aborted check inside the loop. Its call to call.transport.send runs as an argument before untilAborted. untilAborted then does `return onAbort()` on an aborted signal and never attaches a handler to `run`. One qualification: a real fetch already given an aborted signal rejects with AbortError, which is the case the finding describes. My snippet used a plain async send that throws, which has the same effect.

confirmed.title: Rest-day calorie pin can drop below the revision's own recorded floors (80 g carb floor vs 100 g)
confirmed.defect: Pinned targets go through adjustCalories, which uses FLOORS.carbsRest = 80 g (lib/types.ts:377-381, lib/scaling.ts:29-31). The same revision stores carbGMin = 100 and kcalMin = 4*protein + 450 + 400 (lib/profile/derive.ts:164-170, lib/profile/energy.ts:59,203). A rest-day pin therefore produces a day under the revision's own recorded carb and calorie floors. Nothing re-checks the pinned result against those floors. Pins accepted by the settings schema (app/api/targets/route.ts:60-62) and the coach (min 1000) can be as low as 800 kcal.
confirmed.failureScenario: Female, 1968, 170 cm, 72.6 kg, moderate, recomp, restKcal pin 900. I ran deriveTargetRevision and got rest = {protein 145, carbs 80, fat 50, kcal 1350}, while the stored floors say kcalMin 1430 and carbGMin 100. The account ends up 80 kcal under its own minimum and 20 g under its own carb floor. Later checks that read these floors, such as the weekly proposal's applyFloors, disagree with the day that was written.
confirmed.evidence: derive.ts:60-75 macrosWithPins -> adjustCalories(baseline, kcalPin, category); scaling.ts:29-31 carbFloorFor('rest') = FLOORS.carbsRest = 80; derive.ts:164-170 floors.carbGMin = 100 and kcalMin = derived.rate.kcalMin. Reproduced via a temporary vitest file (since removed).
votes:
confirmed: The code matches the finding. I did not re-run the reproduction.

- `macrosWithPins` (lib/profile/derive.ts:60-75) sends pins through `adjustCalories`. That function uses `carbFloorFor('rest')`, which is `FLOORS.carbsRest` = 80 (lib/scaling.ts:29-31, lib/types.ts:377-381).
- `deriveTargetRevision` then stores floors `carbGMin: PROFILE_CARB_G_MIN` (100) and `kcalMin: derived.rate.kcalMin`. The latter is 4·protein + 450 + 400. Nothing re-checks the pinned result against those stored floors.
- The `/api/targets` settings schema (app/api/targets/route.ts:55-56) accepts `restKcal` anywhere from 800 to 6000.
- The settings-pin paths reach `deriveTargetRevision` unfloored: lib/server/targets.ts:155/170/192 and lib/server/target-recompute.ts:285/314.
- The manual-authoring path `authorTargets` does clamp: `Math.max(req.kcalRest, floors.kcalMin)` at lib/server/targets.ts:340. That guard does not cover the derive-with-pins path.
- I found no owner ruling in docs/decisions or docs/audit that accepts a pin below the revision's own floors.
- `grep -rniE` over docs/decisions, docs/audit and docs/specs for "pin … below/under … floor/minimum" returned nothing. The 80 g figure is the old PRD §7.5 hard floor, which the later per-account 100 g floor superseded without aligning the pin path.

Impact: the failure only occurs when a user deliberately pins a rest-day figure below roughly 1430 kcal (for this profile). That limits it to medium. The result is a revision whose numbers sit under its own recorded floors, and downstream readers such as lib/proposal.ts applyFloors disagree with the stored day.

confirmed: Reproduced. A tsx snippet calling applyTargetPins with a rest pin of 900 kcal gave rest = {protein 145, carbs 80, fat 50, kcal 1350}. adjustCalories uses FLOORS.carbsRest = 80 (lib/scaling.ts carbFloorFor, lib/types.ts). deriveTargetRevision stores carbGMin = 100 (PROFILE_CARB_G_MIN) and kcalMin = 4*protein + 450 + 400 = 1430 for the same revision. The pin schema allows 800 kcal and nothing re-checks the pinned result against those floors, so the rest day lands 20 g under the carb floor and about 80 kcal under kcalMin. I found no owner ruling accepting this. The impact is bounded: a pin is user-authored, and the scaling function reports the clamp at its own floors. Severity stays medium or low-medium.

confirmed.title: Maintain/recomp account with an adaptive or proposal revision never switches to standard protein when kidney disease is added
confirmed.defect: The owner decision says kidney disease means standard protein (0.8 g/kg), and a conditions write re-derives at once. The re-derive only reaches a held account in two cases. Case one is the neutralise branch (lines 264-271), which needs hasPace(active) or a paced future revision. Case two is the normal derive branch, which first skips any active revision whose formula_name is not 'profile-energy-v1' (lines 290-293). Adaptive revisions are written as 'adaptive-expenditure-v1' by approve_target_proposal.
confirmed.failureScenario: A recomp or maintain user (pace is always 0) approves a weekly proposal, so the active revision is formula 'adaptive-expenditure-v1' with 2.0 g/kg protein. She then adds 'kidney disease' in Foods > Avoids. recomputeAfterHoldChange runs, hasPace(active) is false, and the formula check returns 'authoritative_formula'. The protein target stays at the high-protein number. buildProposal keeps the authored protein (lib/proposal.ts:129), so every later proposal keeps it too.
confirmed.evidence: target-recompute.ts:264-271 (held branch only acts when paced.length > 0), 290-293 (skip authoritative_formula), supabase/migrations/20261023090500_approve_proposal_via_revision.sql:59 (formula_name 'adaptive-expenditure-v1'), lib/proposal.ts:129 (protein never moves).
votes: confirmed: The code matches the finding. In lib/server/target-recompute.ts plan(), the held branch builds `paced` only from revisions where hasPace() is true. A maintain or recomp account has a 0 pace, so `paced` is empty and the branch is skipped. The next check returns `authoritative_formula` for any active revision whose formula_name is not the profile formula or whose target_source is not derived/manual, and that covers adaptive and proposal revisions. recomputeAfterHoldChange (called from the constraints route) therefore writes nothing, and the 2.0 g/kg protein stays in force. lib/proposal.ts keeps the authored protein ("protein never moves"), so later proposals keep it too. The proposal approval guard in lib/server/proposals.ts only checks paceAllowed and the minor rule. Nothing checks standardProtein, so approving a proposal does not fix it either. The only kidney-protein handling is in the derive path (derive.ts, which sets proteinStandard when standardProtein(eligibility) is true), and this skip prevents it from running for these accounts. The existing test (tests/targets/hold-paths.test.ts, "a hold on an adaptive revision") covers only a paced adaptive revision. I found no kidney-protein test for a 0-pace adaptive revision and no owner ruling accepting this gap. The AGENTS.md text says a conditions write re-derives at once and kidney disease takes standard protein, but the implementation only does that for paced revisions. The finding is real as a health-safety gap. I rate it medium because it needs an adaptive revision, a 0-pace goal, and kidney disease added afterwards.

confirmed: Traced by code reading; not run. A recomp or maintain account has goal_rate_bp_week = 0. Its active revision is adaptive or proposal, so formula_name is 'adaptive-expenditure-v1', not TARGET_FORMULA_NAME ('profile-energy-v1'). Adding kidney disease in Foods > Avoids calls recomputeAfterHoldChange. In plan(), held is true. The neutralise branch (target-recompute.ts:264-271) needs a paced revision, and hasPace() is false for this account, so paced is empty and the branch is skipped. Control then reaches the formula check at lines 290-293, which returns skip 'authoritative_formula'. No standard-protein (0.8 g/kg) revision is written. The later paths do not repair it. proposals.ts only checks pace (paceAllowed) and never checks standardProtein. buildProposal (lib/proposal.ts:129) keeps the authored protein ('protein never moves'). So the high-protein target stays in force for a kidney-disease account, which breaks the owner rule that kidney disease means standard protein. Severity medium fits: it needs a specific account state, but it is a safety-rule miss that never self-corrects.

confirmed.title: Authored (pinned) target write accepts any goalRateBpWeek, bypassing goal presets
confirmed.defect: authoredSchema allows goalRateBpWeek as any integer from -200 to 200 (app/api/targets/route.ts:33-34), unlike the derive path, which refines it with validateRate. authorTargets writes it straight into target_profiles.goal_rate_bp_week (targets.ts:378-379). The only gate is paceAllowed. The value is not checked against the account's goal or the RATE_PRESETS_BP.
confirmed.failureScenario: POST /api/targets with mode 'grams', valid kcal values and goalRateBpWeek -200 for an account whose goal is 'maintain', or a 'gain_muscle' account with -200. The revision stores -200. buildProposal then calls rateTarget with that rate (lib/proposal.ts:111-116) and proposes a weekly deficit of up to 20% of TDEE against the stated goal. The preset set (-25/-50/-75) is bypassed. The wrong-sign pace feeds the weekly proposal, so the user sees the opposite of their goal.
confirmed.evidence: route.ts:33-34 (z.number().int().min(-200).max(200), no validateRate), targets.ts:378-379 (req.goalRateBpWeek ?? active.goal_rate_bp_week ?? 0), versus route.ts:70-73 where the derive path applies validateRate.
votes:
confirmed: The gap is real. In app/api/targets/route.ts, authoredSchema takes goalRateBpWeek as any integer from -200 to 200 with no validateRate check. The derive path refines it through settingsWithRateSchema. authorTargets in lib/server/targets.ts then stores `req.goalRateBpWeek ?? active.goal_rate_bp_week ?? 0` whenever paceAllowed is true. It does not compare the rate with the account's goal or with RATE_PRESETS_BP. buildProposal in lib/proposal.ts feeds active.goal_rate_bp_week straight into rateTarget, so a wrong-sign rate such as -200 on a maintain or gain_muscle account would shape later proposals. I found no guard upstream and no owner ruling that accepts this.

Severity is lower than medium, for four reasons:
1. No in-repo client sends goalRateBpWeek on the authored body. lib/targets/client.ts and tests/targets/targets-route.test.ts only send it inside the derive settings. Only a hand-crafted direct API call reaches this path.
2. The caller is the authenticated owner changing their own account, with no cross-account effect.
3. rateTarget caps the deficit at 20% and the surplus at 10%. The kcal floors and maxWeeklyKcalStep (default 150) bound each proposal. The paceAllowed hold still forces 0 for pregnancy, eating disorder, kidney disease, clinician diets and minors.
4. A proposal still has to be approved.

Fix: validate the rate against the account's stored goal in the authored path, or drop the field from authoredSchema.

confirmed: The validation gap is real. authoredSchema (app/api/targets/route.ts:33) accepts any integer from -200 to 200 for goalRateBpWeek, with no validateRate check against the goal. authorTargets (lib/server/targets.ts:378-379) writes `req.goalRateBpWeek ?? active.goal_rate_bp_week ?? 0` straight into target_profiles. It never reads the goal and only gates on paceAllowed (the pace-hold check). The database does not catch it either. The only goal_rate_bp_week CHECK constraint (20261029090000_rate_goals.sql:21) is on user_settings, and target_profiles has none. buildProposal (lib/proposal.ts:111-116) then passes active.goal_rate_bp_week into rateTarget unchanged. I traced this by reading the code and did not run a repro. Severity is low, not medium, because: (1) only the account's own authenticated user can send the value, so the exposure is self-inflicted; (2) proposals still move by at most max_weekly_kcal_step (default 150 kcal) per week, are held to the kcal and macro minimums, and need the user's approval; (3) the "up to 20% weekly deficit" in the finding is not reachable in one step; (4) the normal pin path appears not to send an off-preset rate, since the finding's own evidence shows only the derive path validating. The fix is to refine the authored path with validateRate against the account's stored goal, or to reject any rate the revision's goal does not list.

confirmed.title: BMR age uses the local-time year while the effective date is a noon-UTC instant
confirmed.defect: bmr computes age with today.getFullYear() (local time). derive.ts effectiveDate builds noon UTC, and the other date logic in the same file (katchEligible, isoDay) uses UTC fields. Where the process zone is UTC+13 or UTC+14, noon UTC on Dec 31 is already Jan 1 locally.
confirmed.failureScenario: A phone in Pacific/Auckland (NZDT, +13) derives or previews targets for effective date 2026-12-31. The Mifflin age is year 2027 minus birth year, which is one year older than the UTC server computes for the same revision. BMR differs by 5 kcal and the frozen seed (bmrKcal, initialTdeeKcal) differs between phone and server. Server-side recompute then rewrites the revision once because revisionMatches sees the difference.
confirmed.evidence: energy.ts:140 uses getFullYear(); energy.ts:107 and derive.ts:84-87 use UTC; rate-eligibility.ts:131 ageOn uses the date string's year.
votes: confirmed: The defect is real but narrow. lib/profile/energy.ts:140 uses today.getFullYear(), which reads the process time zone. The callers pass noon-UTC Dates: derive.ts effectiveDate builds `${value}T12:00:00.000Z`, and lib/server/profile-tdee.ts passes a noon-UTC date too. katchEligible in the same file deliberately uses UTC fields because of that convention. I ran `TZ=Pacific/Auckland node -e` on 2026-12-31T12:00Z and getFullYear() returned 2027. A phone in UTC+12 to +14 therefore gets Mifflin age one year higher than a UTC server for an effective date of Dec 31. That gives a 5 kcal BMR difference and a different frozen seed (derive.ts:151 calls bmr). I found no guard that stops it. No test pins the zone, and no ruling in docs/decisions accepts local-year age. Impact is small: it needs an effective date of exactly Dec 31 plus a UTC+12 to +14 zone. The server revision is authoritative, and the one-off rewrite is self-correcting. The fix is a one-line change to today.getUTCFullYear().

confirmed: I reproduced it with a tsx snippet. Input: a male profile, 70 kg, 170 cm, birth year 1990, and the effective date 2026-12-31T12:00:00Z (the noon-UTC value derive.ts effectiveDate builds). With TZ=UTC, bmr() returns 1587.5. With TZ=Pacific/Auckland, getFullYear() gives 2027 and bmr() returns 1582.5. That is a 5 kcal gap from one year of age. lib/profile/energy.ts:140 is the only local-time year read in the BMR path. katchEligible in the same file uses UTC fields. derive.ts reads bmr(profile, date) at lines 151-152 to freeze bmrKcal. A phone running in a UTC+13 or UTC+14 zone therefore freezes a different seed than the UTC server, which can trigger a server-side rewrite via revisionMatches. The effect is small: 5 kcal, only for effective dates on Dec 31 and only in UTC+13/+14 zones. The fix is to use getUTCFullYear().

confirmed.title: gramsFor multiplies qty by a matched portion's gram weight and ignores the amount in the portion label
confirmed.defect: Catalog portion descriptions are built by import-fdc.py portion_label as '<amount> <unit> <description> <modifier>', for example '0.5 cup', '2 tbsp' or '3 oz'. matchPortion matches only on the unit word and returns the first portion containing it. gramsFor then returns qty * portion.gramWeight, treating every matched portion as 'one unit'. The gram_weight is the weight of the labelled amount, not of one unit.
confirmed.failureScenario: A food whose first 'cup' portion is '0.5 cup' (gram_weight 120) is captured as '1 cup'. gramsFor returns 120 g instead of about 240 g, so the logged calories are halved. A first 'tbsp' portion of '2 tbsp' (30 g) makes '1 tbsp' log as 30 g instead of 15 g, double. Verified: gramsFor(1,'cup',[{description:'1/2 cup',gramWeight:120}],{a:1}) returns 120.
confirmed.evidence: const portion = matchPortion(want, portions); if (portion) return qty * portion.gramWeight;  // matchPortion: p.description.toLowerCase().split(/[^a-z]+/) keeps only letters, so the leading amount is discarded. portion_label puts the amount first in the description.
confirmed.fix: Parse the leading amount from the portion description (digits, decimals and fractions, defaulting to 1) and return qty * gramWeight / amount. Alternatively prefer a portion whose amount is 1 when matching.
votes: confirmed: The defect is real in the code. import-fdc.py portion_label builds the description as "<amount> <unit> <description> <modifier>", so the catalog_portions label carries the amount and gram_weight is the weight of that whole amount. matchPortion splits the description on non-letters, which drops the leading number. gramsFor then returns qty * gramWeight with no division by the label amount. The path is live: lib/server/capture.ts:308-311 loads catalog_portions rows (description, gram_weight) and passes them to gramsFor and matchPortion, so the grams, and the calories derived from them, are wrong for grounded capture items. The only test fixtures (tests/capture/quantity.test.ts) use amount-1 labels ("1 cup, cooked", "1 slice", "1 whole"), which is why they pass. No upstream guard normalizes per-unit weights, and I found no owner ruling or audit that accepts the behaviour. The size of the effect depends on the data. FDC rows with amount other than 1 (such as "0.5 cup", "2 tbsp" or "3 oz") are the ones that give wrong grams. I did not run the code or check how often such rows occur in the real catalog. I have not rechecked severity; medium is plausible.

confirmed: Reproduced with tsx: gramsFor(1,"cup",[{description:"0.5 cup",gramWeight:120}]) returns 120 and gramsFor(1,"tbsp",[{description:"2 tbsp",gramWeight:30}]) returns 30. The causes are the ones named. matchPortion matches only letter words, and gramsFor returns qty * gramWeight. portion_label in scripts/import-fdc.py puts the FDC amount first in the label, and gram_weight is the weight of that whole amount. The path is live, since lib/server/capture.ts:310 calls it for captured foods. I lowered severity to low because the labelled amount is usually 1. Most USDA SR Legacy portions read "1 cup", "1 tbsp" and so on, so the error only hits foods whose first matching portion has an amount other than 1, such as some Foundation or FNDDS rows. The UI paths (gramsForPortion) share the same one-unit assumption, and I found no owner ruling that accepts it. I did not measure how many catalog rows have an amount other than 1, so I cannot say how often the bug occurs.

confirmed.title: Capture invents 100 g per 'whole' or 'piece' for any matched catalog food, despite the module's refuse-to-guess contract
confirmed.defect: quantity.ts says an amount with no gram weight must return null so the item goes to the stepper. gramsFor does return qty * DEFAULT_WHOLE_GRAMS for 'whole' or 'piece' when per100g has any key. capture.ts passes a dummy per100g of { energy_kcal: 0 }, so that guard is always true. Any catalog food with no matching portion gets a fabricated 100 g per count.
confirmed.failureScenario: The user says 'two bananas' and the picked revision has no portion containing the word 'whole' or 'piece'. grams becomes 200 and is logged as a measured amount. A real banana weighs about 118 g, so the snapshot kcal and macros are about 15% too low. 'a pumpkin', 'a whole pizza' or 'a watermelon' land at 100 g, wrong by a factor of 10 or more, and look measured with no unknown mark.
confirmed.evidence: gramsFor(amount.qty, amount.unit, portions, { energy_kcal: 0 }) ?? item.grams;  and  if ((want === "whole" || want === "piece") && Object.keys(per100g).length > 0) return qty * DEFAULT_WHOLE_GRAMS;
confirmed.fix: Pass the real per-100g map (or drop the default) and return null for a count with no portion, so the item falls to the stepper or the unknown-mass path. Or flag the invented weight as an estimate.
votes:
confirmed: The mechanism is real and reachable. lib/server/capture.ts:310 calls gramsFor(amount.qty, amount.unit, portions, { energy_kcal: 0 }). The dummy per100g always has a key, so the guard `Object.keys(per100g).length > 0` in lib/capture/quantity.ts:85 is always true. Any whole or piece amount with no portion description containing the word "whole" or "piece" (matchPortion needs an exact word match) therefore gets qty * 100 g. parseAmount also turns every bare count ("two eggs", "a pumpkin") into unit "whole". That result replaces the model's own item.grams estimate, because `?? item.grams` only runs when gramsFor returns null. So the model's roughly 118 g for a banana or its large estimate for a pumpkin is overwritten by a flat 100 g per count. SR-style portion rows are usually "1 medium", "1 large" or "1 cup", so the no-"whole" case is common. Nothing marks the result as unknown. Portion follow-ups key off the model's low-confidence items, not the server's grams, and the item stays grounded with grams set.

Weakness in the finding: its premise that the module "refuses to guess" is only partly right. The file header says vague measures return null. The comment in gramsFor, however, says a count of a whole food has a defensible default. quantity.test.ts:52 pins "falls back to 100 g only when per100g is known" as intended. The real bug is the dummy per100g defeating that intended guard, and the 100 g default overwriting a better model estimate. The user also sees the draft on a review sheet before anything is logged, which limits the damage. Medium severity fits.

No owner ruling in docs/decisions or docs/audit accepts this behaviour. The grep hits there were unrelated.

confirmed: Reproduced. In lib/server/capture.ts:310 the call is gramsFor(qty, unit, portions, { energy_kcal: 0 }), and the dummy per100g makes the Object.keys(per100g).length > 0 guard in lib/capture/quantity.ts always true. I ran gramsFor(2, "whole", [{description:"1 cup, sliced", gramWeight:150}], {energy_kcal:0}) after parseAmount("2 whole bananas") and got 200. That 100 g per count then replaces the model's own item.grams, because the ?? fallback never fires. The fabricated weight is stored as grams with no unknown mark. The quantity.ts header says an amount with no gram weight should return null, and the in-function comment calls the default "defensible". That default is only defensible if the guard checks real nutrition data, which it does not here. I found no owner ruling that accepts this. I restored the repo; git status is clean.

confirmed.title: Recipe nutrient maths ignores energy_kcal_calc, so the one energy rule is not applied to recipe totals and the logged recipe item
confirmed.defect: computeRecipeNutrients, and its SQL twin in 20260919090300_phase3_sync_entities.sql, sum energy_kcal and energy_kcal_calc as independent codes. Coverage and 'complete' are judged on energy_kcal only. An ingredient that has only the Atwater-calculated energy, which is how the catalog stores foods USDA did not measure, counts as having no energy. The recipe's energy_kcal becomes the sum of only the ingredients that carry a measured value. The recipe's loggable user_food per_100g carries both energy_kcal (partial) and energy_kcal_calc (the rest). itemEnergy then prefers the partial reported value.
confirmed.failureScenario: A recipe has ingredient A (energy_kcal 100 per serving) and ingredient B (energy_kcal_calc 80 only). Recipe energy_kcal is 100 and energy_kcal_calc is 80. Logging it gives a snapshot where itemEnergy picks reported = 100. The day total and rings count 100 instead of 180. The recipe is flagged partial, but the number is still an undercount of what the energy rule would give for the same data. The recipe card's 'at least N kcal' is also lower than the calculated figure.
confirmed.evidence: measured.set(code, ...) is per literal code. coverage = Math.min(...TRACKED_MACROS.map(code => measured.get(code)/items.length)) where TRACKED_MACROS has MACRO_CODES.kcal = energy_kcal only. SQL: unnest(array['energy_kcal','protein','carbohydrate','fat_total','fiber_total']). Neither side falls back per item to energy_kcal_calc as lib/nutrients/energy.ts itemEnergy does.
confirmed.fix: In the recipe sum, select each ingredient snapshot's energy with the energy rule (reported, else calculated) before summing, store it as the recipe's energy_kcal, and count it toward energy coverage. Change the SQL twin the same way (a new migration).
votes: confirmed: The mechanism holds in code. In lib/recipes/nutrients.ts, computeRecipeNutrients keeps a separate sum and a separate measured count for each literal nutrient code. TRACKED_MACROS holds energy_kcal only (MACRO_CODES.kcal), so coverage ignores energy_kcal_calc. The SQL twin in 20260919090300_phase3_sync_entities.sql does the same: its unnest list names only 'energy_kcal'. It also sums per code from compute_item_snapshot, which emits energy_kcal and energy_kcal_calc as separate keys, with a null amount when the source lacks a value. Calc-only foods are real. fdc-map.ts and off-map.ts always set energy_kcal_calc to the Atwater figure, while energy_kcal is null when the source gives none. The recipe's loggable user_food per_100g is built from every key in v_per_serving. It therefore carries a partial energy_kcal (100 in the example) alongside energy_kcal_calc (80). lib/nutrients/energy.ts itemEnergy takes reported when it is a finite number >= 0. A logged serving therefore counts 100, not 180. I found no owner ruling in docs/decisions or docs/audit that accepts this, and no recipe test covers energy_kcal_calc. Two things limit the severity. The recipe is already marked partial, because coverage is below 1 on energy_kcal. The coverage audit (#21) records that a partial recipe kcal is "at least N", and migration 20261210090400 stamps nutrition_partial on the logged item. The undercount is therefore disclosed, not silent. It also needs an ingredient with only Atwater energy, which is uncommon in USDA SR data. confirmed.title: Failed apply permanently swallows the payload: a retry is answered 'duplicate'
confirmed.defect: applyIngest records the ingest event (health_ingest_event, status 'applied', unique on source_id+payload_hash) BEFORE health_ingest_apply runs, in separate RPC calls with no compensation. If the apply RPC errors (timeout, transient 5xx, deploy window), the route returns 500 but the event row stays. The exporter's retry of the identical body hits ON CONFLICT, gets is_new=false and is returned as status 'duplicate' with 0 accepted, without applying.
confirmed.failureScenario: Health Auto Export or a Shortcut posts a day of steps, weight and sleep. health_ingest_apply fails with a statement timeout, so the client gets 500 and retries the same body, as HAE does. The retry returns 200 {status:'duplicate', accepted:0}. The samples never reach health_samples, and every identical resend is dropped the same way. Weight, steps and sleep for that window are lost until the content changes.
confirmed.evidence: lib/server/health-ingest.ts: event RPC at ~L88; `if (!row.is_new) return {status:'duplicate',...}` at ~L96; apply RPC and its `throw new HttpError(500, ...)` at ~L103-105, with no delete or flag of the event on failure. SQL health_ingest_event (20260925000000_phase5_health_ingest.sql) flips status to 'duplicate' on conflict. tests/health/ingest-route.test.ts only covers a genuine repeat, not a failed apply.
confirmed.fix: Make event creation and apply one transaction (a single RPC), or on apply failure delete the event row (or mark it 'failed'). Treat a duplicate as a skip only when the existing event completed. Oura's pullTwoDays already ignores is_new and re-applies, so apply is idempotent and a safe model.

votes:
confirmed: The mechanism is real and nothing in the checkout guards against it. applyIngest in lib/server/health-ingest.ts (L97-105) calls the health_ingest_event RPC first, as its own call. That RPC inserts into ingest_events with status 'applied', unique on (source_id, payload_hash). It then calls health_ingest_apply as a separate RPC, and nothing joins the two in one transaction.

If the apply RPC fails, the code throws HttpError 500 and does not delete or flag the event row. The route in app/api/health/ingest/route.ts has no compensation either. payloadHash is sha256 of JSON.stringify(body), so an identical resend produces the same hash. On that retry, health_ingest_event hits ON CONFLICT, flips status to 'duplicate' and returns is_new=false (xmax != 0). applyIngest then returns {status:'duplicate', accepted:0} with HTTP 200 and never calls apply. Every identical resend is dropped the same way.

I found no later migration that changes this, and no owner ruling accepts it. Nothing in docs/decisions or docs/audit says this behaviour is intended. An earlier Sol review of the Phase 10 spec (docs/audit/specs/2026-09-22-phase-10-r1-gpt6-sol.md item 8) flagged the same flaw and asked for atomic or recoverable registration. I found nothing in the code showing it was fixed.

Two conditions limit how often it fires. The apply RPC has to fail, which is a rare timeout, 5xx or deploy window. The exporter has to resend a byte-identical body. HAE and Shortcut resends of the same export satisfy the second.

Severity: the failure is silent data loss, but the trigger is rare and a changed payload recovers it. Medium is arguably fairer than high, but I'm leaving the severity as reported.

confirmed.title: Oura 401 'refresh then retry' never actually refreshes the token
confirmed.defect: pullTwoDays passes ouraGet a `refresh` callback that calls accessTokenFor(admin, source) with the same stale `source` object. accessTokenFor only exchanges the refresh token when expires_at is within the 5-minute skew. For a token that Oura rejects with 401 while the stored expires_at is still in the future, the callback returns the identical access_token, the retry gets a second 401, and `refreshed` is already true, so ouraGet throws 'Oura <path> failed with 401'.
confirmed.failureScenario: The stored expires_at is later than reality (Oura invalidated the access token early, or the expiry was computed from Date.now()+expires_in after a slow exchange). Every daily cron pull and the post-connect pull fail with 401 until the clock passes expires_at, so Oura data stops updating for that user. Spec section 7 promises exactly one refresh-then-retry on 401.
confirmed.evidence: oura.ts: `refresh: async () => accessTokenFor(admin, source, { fetchFn })`; accessTokenFor: `if (Date.parse(current.expires_at) - now.getTime() > OURA_REFRESH_SKEW_MS) return current.access_token;`. oura/client.ts: 401 path calls opts.refresh() once, then rethrows.
confirmed.fix: Give accessTokenFor a `force` flag (or a separate refreshTokens function) that skips the expiry check. Have the 401 callback call it and use the rotated pair.
votes: confirmed: The code matches the finding. In lib/server/oura.ts, pullTwoDays gives ouraGet a refresh callback that calls accessTokenFor with the same stale `source`. accessTokenFor returns the stored access_token unchanged whenever expires_at is more than the 5-minute skew away. It does not force a refresh-token exchange. In lib/oura/client.ts, a 401 triggers one refresh call and then retries. If the retry also returns 401, `refreshed` is already true and the status is not retryable, so ouraGet throws "Oura <path> failed with 401". A token that Oura has revoked or expired early, while the stored expires_at is still in the future, therefore never gets refreshed. This conflicts with the spec section 7 promise of one refresh-then-retry on 401. A second problem: pullTwoDays fires three ouraGet calls in parallel, and they share one stale source. If the token were forced to rotate, they would race on the refresh-token exchange, and the compare-and-set update on `oauth` would only let one of them store the new pair. I found no guard upstream, no owner ruling, and no audit note that accepts this. The impact is limited to an edge case where the stored expiry is later than the real one. It would persist until the clock passes expires_at, which is why I rate it medium. I did not run the tests.

confirmed: I confirmed this by reading the code path; I did not run a repro. In lib/server/oura.ts, pullTwoDays calls accessTokenFor once, then passes ouraGet a refresh callback that calls accessTokenFor with the same stale `source` object. accessTokenFor returns current.access_token whenever the stored expires_at is more than OURA_REFRESH_SKEW_MS in the future, so it makes no refresh_token exchange. In lib/oura/client.ts the 401 branch runs once: it sets refreshed=true, calls opts.refresh(), and gets the same token back. The retry returns a second 401, the branch is skipped because refreshed is true, 401 is not retryable, and the client throws "Oura <path> failed with 401". So the spec's "refresh then retry once on 401" does not refresh in this case. Real refreshes still happen when expires_at is within the 5-minute skew, and the stored expiry would have to be later than what Oura actually enforces for this to trigger. It also stops by itself once the clock passes expires_at, because the next pull then takes the refresh path. Because it needs a mismatch between the stored expiry and Oura's real expiry, and Oura is a supplementary integration, I rate it low rather than medium. A fix would force a refresh in the callback, for example an accessTokenFor option that skips the expiry check. The three parallel ouraGet calls would also need to share one refresh. I found no owner ruling that accepts this behaviour. The 2026-09-13 audit covered a different Oura issue, the compare-and-swap rotation race.

confirmed.title: Oura sleep, resting HR, HRV and readiness are bucketed by UTC day, not the user's day
confirmed.defect: ouraSleepToSamples (and the readiness timestamp path) stamp real instants with tz DEFAULT_TZ ('UTC'). mergedDays buckets each sample with localDateOf(start_time, sample.tz), so a sleep period that starts at 23:00 local in UTC+1 or later zones lands on the previous calendar day of wake time. The code comment says UTC is only for synthetic day windows, not real instants, and the Oura bedtime_start string carries the real offset.
confirmed.failureScenario: A user in Berlin or Tokyo sleeps 23:00 to 07:00 local. Oura sleep, lowest_heart_rate and average_hrv are filed under the day BEFORE the wake day. HAE sleep for the same night is bucketed by the user's zone (also the start day), so Oura and Apple data disagree on which day a night belongs to. The Today and Body cards then show last night's sleep, RHR and HRV one day stale or on the wrong date. Because the Oura sleep winner replaces Apple's, a user with both gets the wrong day's number.
confirmed.evidence: map.ts: `out.push(sample(d.id, "sleep_asleep", asleep, "s", start, end, DEFAULT_TZ))` and the same for time_in_bed, lowest_heart_rate, average_hrv; readiness real-timestamp branch also uses DEFAULT_TZ; health-daily.ts mergedDays: `localDateOf(sample.start_time, sample.tz)`.
confirmed.fix: Take the zone/offset from the Oura bedtime_start string (or the account's stored time_zone) when mapping sleep-derived samples, and bucket sleep by wake day as Oura's `day` field does.
votes:
confirmed: The core defect is real, but the finding's scenario is mis-stated. lib/oura/map.ts stamps every real-instant sleep sample (sleep_asleep, sleep_in_bed, resting_heart_rate, hrv_sdnn) and the readiness sample with a real timestamp using DEFAULT_TZ, which is "UTC". lib/server/oura.ts pullTwoDays passes those samples straight to health_ingest_apply. It never calls healthTimeZone or any user or source zone lookup. HAE ingest does that in lib/server/health-ingest.ts. The RPC stores coalesce(tz,'UTC'). mergedDays then buckets with localDateOf(start_time, sample.tz), so Oura samples are bucketed by UTC day. The Oura sleep winner replaces Apple's for that day, so the wrong-day number wins.

I found no guard, owner ruling or earlier audit accepting this. The only ruling hit, wave4-rulings, covers only the OAuth flow. tests/health/oura-map.test.ts asserts tz equals DEFAULT_TZ. Its comment says the ingest path resolves the user's zone, and that is false for the Oura path.

The finding's example is wrong in direction. A 23:00 bedtime in Berlin or Tokyo is 22:00Z or 14:00Z, the same calendar day, so it is bucketed correctly. The failures are:
- Western zones, e.g. 23:05 EDT is 03:05Z the next day, which the repo's own test shows. A normal bedtime lands on the wake day while HAE puts the same night on the start day.
- Eastern zones, for bedtimes after local midnight, e.g. 02:00 JST is 17:00Z the previous day.

So the Oura and HAE day assignments disagree and the cards show the wrong date. Medium severity fits: there is no data loss, but the wrong day shows on Today and Body.

confirmed: The defect is real, but the stated scenario is wrong. In lib/oura/map.ts, sleep and RHR/HRV samples carry tz DEFAULT_TZ ('UTC'). The readiness branch with a real timestamp does the same. mergedDays then buckets them with localDateOf(start_time, 'UTC'). I ran ouraSleepToSamples through that path in a throwaway vitest file, now removed:
- Berlin 23:00 start: the Oura day is 2026-10-01 and the user-zone day is 2026-10-01. They agree, so the finding's Berlin/Tokyo 23:00 example does not reproduce.
- Tokyo 02:00 start: the Oura day is 2026-10-01 and the user-zone day is 2026-10-02. This is wrong.
- Los Angeles 23:00 start: the Oura day is 2026-10-02 and the user-zone day is 2026-10-01. This is wrong, and it is the common case for US users. Their sleep, RHR and HRV land one day later than Apple/HAE data for the same night.
The mismatch appears whenever the local start time and its UTC instant fall on different calendar dates. That affects all western-hemisphere users with an evening bedtime, and eastern-hemisphere users with an after-midnight bedtime. The tz is never taken from the user's zone or from the offset in bedtime_start. Only the synthetic daily_activity and fallback readiness windows correctly use UTC.

Number("150,5") is NaN, so grams stays at the last valid prefix, 150. A lone "-" or "." gives NaN, and "-5" fails the >= 0 test, so grams keeps its old value. canConfirmPortion (line 52) checks only grams > 0, foodRefId !== null and !submitting. It never looks at gramsText, so Log it stays enabled and logs the stale number while the box shows something else. confirmed.title: Package count can round up one extra package because of float division in Math.ceil
confirmed.defect: buyGrams is computed as Math.ceil(net / packageGrams) * packageGrams. `net` is rounded to 4 decimals, but the division is float, so an exact multiple of a decimal package size can come out as k + 1e-15 and ceil returns k + 1.
confirmed.failureScenario: For a 340.2 g (12 oz) package and a need of exactly 7 packages (2381.4 g), 2381.4 / 340.2 = 7.000000000000001, so ceil gives 8 and the list tells the user to buy 8 packages. The same happens with 170.1 g. I checked with node: [[340.2,7,2381.4,7.000000000000001],[170.1,7,1190.7,7.000000000000001]]. The price estimate inherits it, since it uses Math.ceil(buyGrams / quote.packageGrams).
confirmed.evidence: lib/shopping/aggregate.ts:156 `Math.ceil(net / line.packageGrams) * line.packageGrams`. A node check of multiples of the package sizes 453.6, 226.8, 340.2, 907.2, 28.35, 113.4, 454.5 and 425.25 showed the failure for 340.2 and 170.1.
confirmed.fix: Use Math.ceil(round(net / pkg) - 1e-9) or compare in integer micrograms, as purchase-mass.ts already does with BigInt.
votes: confirmed: The code is as described. lib/shopping/aggregate.ts:156 computes Math.ceil(net / line.packageGrams) * line.packageGrams. lib/shopping/planner.ts:183 has the same expression. `net` is only rounded to 4 decimals. Running Math.ceil(2381.4/340.2) in node gives 8, because the division is 7.000000000000001. I found no epsilon guard and no upstream normalisation of packageGrams. No ruling in docs/decisions or docs/audit accepts this. The effect is that a need that is an exact multiple of a decimal package size lists one extra package, and the price estimate at line 192 inherits it. Impact is small. It fails safe by over-buying one package, and it needs a need that is exactly k times the package size, which is rare with real recipe grams. Low severity is correct. The fix is to ceil with a small tolerance, for example Math.ceil(net / pkg - 1e-9).

confirmed: I reproduced it with node using the repo's own `round`, defined at aggregate.ts:48. For a 340.2 g package and 7 packages' worth of need, `net` is 2381.4, and 2381.4 / 340.2 = 7.000000000000001, so `Math.ceil` gives 8. A 170.1 g package with 1190.7 g of need fails the same way. Line 156 has no epsilon guard, so `buyGrams` is one package too high, and the price estimate inherits that. The failure needs a need that is an exact multiple of a decimal package size, so it is rare and costs the user at most one extra package. The code path is as the finding describes.

confirmed.title: Foundation foods without reported energy fall back to a fiber-subtracted Atwater value, understating kcal by up to 140 per 100 g
confirmed.defect: NUTRIENT_MAP maps only FDC id 1008 to energy_kcal. Foundation foods mostly publish energy as Atwater General (2047) or Specific (2048), and the importer ignores both. The catalog then reads energy_kcal ?? energy_kcal_calc, and energy_kcal_calc (catalog_atwater_kcal) is 4*protein + 4*max(carb - fiber, 0) + 9*fat. That fiber-subtracted number is not the published energy.
confirmed.failureScenario: A user searches the online catalog for a Foundation food such as 'Flour, coconut', 'Flaxseed, ground', 'Nuts, almonds, whole, raw' or 'Bulgur'. The card and logged entry use energy_kcal_calc. I read the 2026-09-12 Foundation CSVs in ~/Backups/usda/fdc. Of 469 foundation_food rows, 334 have no 1008 row. Among the 242 of those that have all three macros plus a 2047/2048 value, the calc is below the published energy by 139.8 kcal/100 g for sorghum bran (263 vs 403), 137 for coconut flour (301 vs 438), 92.5 for ground flaxseed (453 vs 545) and 43 for raw almonds (583 vs 626). Every log of these foods is under-counted, and energy_mismatch can never fire because there is no reported value to compare.
confirmed.evidence: scripts/import-fdc.py:80 (only 1008 -> energy_kcal; no 2047/2048 entry). food_nutrient.csv for fdc_foundation: 1008 on 135 food-nutrient rows against 2047 on 347 and 2048 on 312. Read path: lib/server/catalog.ts:394 `n.energy_kcal ?? n.energy_kcal_calc`. Calc definition: supabase/migrations/20260912090050_catalog_activate.sql:22-24. FNDDS (nutrient_nbr 208 -> 1008) and SR Legacy (1008 on 7,793 rows) are unaffected.
confirmed.fix: Map 2047 (preferring it, else 2048) to energy_kcal for the Foundation source in the importer, in the same way lib/catalog/fdc-map.ts handles duplicate ids. Re-import the Foundation source. Make catalog_atwater_kcal add fiber at 2 kcal/g, or flag foods whose energy comes only from the fallback.
votes: confirmed: The importer's NUTRIENT_MAP in scripts/import-fdc.py only maps FDC id 1008 to energy_kcal, so Foundation foods that publish only 2047/2048 get no reported energy. The import then writes energy_kcal_calc, computed in SQL by catalog_atwater_kcal as 4*protein + 4*max(carb-fiber,0) + 9*fat, and the read path uses it as the fallback. I re-ran the check on ~/Backups/usda/fdc/2026-09-12/fdc_foundation. Of 395 foundation_food ids, 273 have no 1008 row. Among the 227 of those with protein, fat, carbohydrate and a 2047/2048 value, the published energy exceeds the calc by up to 139.8 kcal/100 g, and 34 foods differ by more than 20 kcal. confirmed.defect: realPortionsFor sorts by portionRank and marks index 0 as isDefault. portionRank gives '1 cup', '1 large', '1 oz', '1 slice' and similar the same score of -300, then breaks the tie by label length. confirmed.title: Plan writes (set_slot_meal, add_slot_item, set_slot_item) never check diet-flag or profile hard rules
confirmed.defect: Grounding a plan item judges it with checkItemWithMarks. That function hard-codes preferenceFlags: [] and never passes profileRules. refusePlanBlocked then refuses only items whose verdict is 'blocked' (allergen, banned category, Avoid, pregnancy/tuna). The account's diet flags (vegetarian, vegan, halal, kosher, no_pork, no_beef, no_shellfish and similar, stored in user_settings.diet_prefs.flags) and its confirmed profile hard rules are read only for log_meal (markLoggedActions), save_recipe (filterRecipeActions) and suggestions. No policy pass reads them for plan writes.
confirmed.failureScenario: A vegetarian, halal or no-pork account says 'change my dinner to bacon and eggs for the next two weeks'. Grounding returns verdict 'allowed' with flagged [] for the pork item. refusePlanBlocked keeps the action. The phone's applySetSlotMeal writes it into the plan for up to 31 dates, with no refusal and no mark. The same food would be refused as a recipe ingredient and skipped as a suggestion. This breaks the rule 'a plan never holds a food the account's rules block' (lib/coach/plan-policy.ts header).
confirmed.evidence: lib/coach/policy.ts:94 `evaluatePolicy(profile, { ...itemEvidence(item, profile, false), preferenceFlags: [] })`. lib/coach/actions/ground-kit.ts groundNamedFood calls it (groundItem for set_slot_meal and add_slot_item; groundNamedLine for set_slot_item). lib/server/coach-role-advice.ts:~115-124 applyGroundedActionPolicies runs markLoggedActions (log_meal only), adviseGroundedListActions, filterRecipeActions (save_recipe only: `actions.filter(a => a.kind === 'save_recipe')`, lib/coach/recipe-policy.ts), then refusePlanBlocked. refusePlanBlocked reads only `flagged` (blocked verdicts), lib/coach/plan-policy.ts. confirmed.fix: For set_slot_meal, add_slot_item and set_slot_item, run the log_meal evidence-based policy pass (loadSuggestionEvidence with preferenceFlags and profile facets, evaluatePolicy with facetAction 'exclude' and profileRules) after grounding. Treat any non-allowed result as a refusal in refusePlanBlocked.
votes: confirmed: I read the code and could not refute it. lib/coach/policy.ts:94 checkItemWithMarks passes `preferenceFlags: []` and `itemEvidence(..., false)`, so no profileRules and no diet flags reach evaluatePolicy. ground-kit.ts groundNamedFood uses only that check. `flagged()` lists only items whose verdict is 'blocked'. applyGroundedActionPolicies in lib/server/coach-role-advice.ts then runs markLoggedActions (log only), adviseGroundedListActions, filterRecipeActions (save_recipe only) and refusePlanBlocked, which reads only `flagged`. Diet flags and profile hard rules are loaded only for logging, recipes and suggestions (suggest-policy.ts). A pork item for a vegetarian, halal or no-pork account therefore grounds as 'allowed' and the plan write goes through. I found no ruling in docs/decisions or docs/audit that accepts this. plan-policy.ts says a plan never holds a food the rules block. confirmed.title: OFF 'en:crustaceans' declaration does not count as evidence for the 'crustacean' allergen, so a complete label clears it
confirmed.defect: The alias table sends 'crustaceans' to the combined 'shellfish' key, but 'crustacean shellfish' to the 'crustacean' key. deriveEvidence('crustacean', ...) decides `tagged` by allergenKey(tag) === 'crustacean'. confirmed.failureScenario: A user's profile avoids 'crustacean shellfish' (alias key 'crustacean', FALCPA major allergen). confirmed.title: Fast-path Avoid and Favored marks take a compound food phrase as one food and mark one arbitrary search hit
confirmed.defect: foodMentions captures everything between 'add' or 'put' and 'to my eats/avoid list' as one name, so 'add peanuts and shellfish to my avoid list' yields the single name 'peanuts and shellfish'. foodArgs and the list-mark intent treat this as one deterministic argument with confidence 1. groundListMark then searches that string with limit 1, replaces the name with the top hit's catalog name, and applies one mark. A multi-item instruction is silently reduced to one mark on whichever food ranked first.
confirmed.failureScenario: The user says 'add peanuts and shellfish to my avoid list'. The fast path (no Gemini) grounds one search hit for 'peanuts and shellfish', for example a shellfish row. It replies 'Adding <that food> to your Avoid list.' and writes one membership. The other food is never added, with no clarification. The user believes both allergens are on Avoid. A second instruction in one message ('...avoid list, and take pork off my eats list') is dropped the same way.
confirmed.evidence: lib/server/coach-turn/intent.ts:13-23 regex `(.+?)\s+(?:to|on)\s+...(?:eats|avoid)` returns [name] with no split on 'and' or commas. lib/coach/actions/food-lists.ts:101-103 sets argConfidence { name: 1 }. groundListMark (same file ~68-85) calls ports.searchFoods(userId, input.name, 1) and sets `name: hit.name`. lib/server/coach-turn/fast-path.ts then returns after a single grounded action.
confirmed.fix: In foodMentions, return null (use the model path) when the captured name contains ' and ', ',', '&', or a second verb. Or return one name per item and ground them all.
votes:
confirmed: The code matches the finding. I did not run a test, so the "arbitrary top hit" part rests on code reading alone.

- `foodMentions` in `lib/server/coach-turn/intent.ts:13-23` uses a lazy `(.+?)` capture between "add/put" and "to/on my eats/avoid". It returns `[name]` with no split on "and" or commas. "add peanuts and shellfish to my avoid list" gives the single name "peanuts and shellfish".
- `foodArgs` in `lib/coach/intent-args.ts:82` takes that single string. The list-mark `intent.extract` in `lib/coach/actions/food-lists.ts:101` sets `argConfidence { name: 1 }` whenever any food was mentioned.
- Nothing upstream checks for a compound phrase. A grep of `fast-path.ts`, `intent.ts` and `intent-args.ts` found no split or multi-item handling.
- `groundListMark` (food-lists.ts, about lines 60-80) calls `searchFoods(userId, input.name, 1)`. It then applies one mark under `hit.name`, the top hit's canonical catalog name.
- `groundNamedFood` in `lib/coach/actions/ground-kit.ts` only checks that a hit exists and has a ref. It never checks that the hit matches the whole requested phrase.

So the second allergen is dropped silently. The reply ("Adding <food> to your Avoid list.") does not mention it, and there is no clarification.

I found no owner ruling or audit that accepts this. The only grep hit for "peanuts and" is a research file.

I rate it medium rather than low because the failure leaves an allergen unmarked while the user believes it is on Avoid. The user can see which food was added in the reply, which limits the harm.

confirmed: Ran the regex from lib/server/coach-turn/intent.ts:14 on the message. "add peanuts and shellfish to my avoid list" gives the single name "peanuts and shellfish", with no split on "and" or commas. foodArgs (lib/coach/intent-args.ts:82) takes that one string as the name. food-lists.ts:101-103 sets argConfidence { name: 1 }. groundListMark calls searchFoods(userId, input.name, 1) and overwrites name with hit.name. I found no multi-item or compound guard in intent.ts, fast-path.ts or intent-args.ts. So only one mark is written, with no clarification. For the second scenario ("add peanuts to my avoid list, and take pork off my eats list"), the first pattern matches and returns just "peanuts". confirmed.title: Compound quantities are read as the first number, so the fast path applies the wrong amount
confirmed.defect: NUMBER_RE and extractNumbers read 'an hour', 'a cup' and '1/2 cup' as separate fixed numbers. 'An hour and a half' becomes 1 hour, 'a cup and a half' becomes 1 cup, '1/2 cup' becomes the numbers '1' and '2 cup', and '1 hour 30 minutes' becomes two numbers. With exactly one unit-bearing number, measuredNumber gives confidence 1. With two, it trusts Jev's which_number pick, but the answer is a sum that no single candidate holds. The fast path still clears the 0.90 argument threshold and applies the action with no model turn.

'Log 1/2 cup of water' extracts '1' (no unit) and '2 cup'. If Jev picks '2 cup' at 0.9 or more, 2 cups (480 ml) are logged instead of half a cup. 'Move meals 1 hour 30 minutes later' makes Jev pick either '1 hour' or '30 minutes', so 60 or 30 minutes are applied instead of 90.
confirmed.evidence: Reproduced with extractNumbers: 'push my meals back an hour and a half' gives [{value:1,unit:'hour',raw:'an hour'}]; 'log 1/2 cup of water' gives [{1,null,'1'},{2,'cup','2 cup'}]; 'a cup and a half' gives [{1,'cup','a cup'}]; 'move meals 1 hour 30 minutes later' gives [{1,'hour'},{30,'min'}]. lib/coach/intent-args.ts measuredNumber:52-60 and isFastPathEligible in lib/coach/intent.ts accept these.

confirmed: I reproduced it with tsx. extractNumbers("push my meals back an hour and a half") returns only [{1, hour, "an hour"}]. extractNumbers("log 1/2 cup of water") returns [{1, null, "1"}, {2, cup, "2 cup"}]. Nothing downstream catches it. shift_schedule's intent.extract in lib/coach/actions/shift-schedule.ts:61-82 calls measuredNumber. With exactly one number, measuredNumber returns confidence 1. With two, it returns whatever confidence Jev gave its which_number pick, and neither candidate holds the true sum or fraction. isFastPathEligible in lib/coach/intent.ts:211 checks only the argument-confidence floor and that nothing is missing. So the fast path applies 60 minutes for "an hour and a half". For "1/2 cup" it can log 2 cups if Jev picks "2 cup".

I found no tests or owner rulings in docs/decisions or docs/audit that accept this. The 7-day coach Undo limits the damage, but the applied amount is still wrong. Severity medium stands.

confirmed: I ran extractNumbers on the four phrases and got the outputs the finding describes. "an hour and a half" gives one number, {1, hour, "an hour"}. "a cup and a half" gives {1, cup}. "log 1/2 cup of water" gives {1, null, "1"} and {2, cup, "2 cup"}. "1 hour 30 minutes" gives {1, hour} and {30, min}. The regex has no handling for "and a half" or for fractions.

A grep of lib, app and components finds LABEL_FOOD_PLACEHOLDER_REF and label_food only in server code and server tests, so no client code sends either. With the default toggle, the label commit always fails with 422. The user must turn the toggle off to log at all. The path that saves a label as the user's own food cannot be reached from the client. canSave requires a foodRefId per kept item, so an ungrounded novel label item can't be saved either. I did not run a repro snippet; the trace is fully static and every hop is visible in the code.

confirmed.title: Offline barcode match replays a stale cached policy verdict for up to 30 days
confirmed.defect: offlineMatch rebuilds a BarcodeMatch from the IndexedDB cache using cached.policy, the allowed/blocked/unverified verdict computed on the server under the rules at the time of the original scan. The cache is kept for SCAN_CACHE_RETENTION_DAYS = 30. Nothing re-evaluates it against the account's current allergens, Avoid marks, categories or conditions.
confirmed.failureScenario: A user scans a granola bar while online and it is 'allowed'. Later she adds a peanut allergy or marks the brand Avoid. Offline, she rescans the same bar. offlineMatch returns the old 'allowed' verdict and allergenTags, so the confirm sheet shows no warning for a product that now conflicts with her rules. The commit is queued offline and never gets a server `flagged` mark (see the next finding).
confirmed.evidence: lib/barcode/client.ts:171 `policy: cached.policy ?? { verdict: 'unverified' }`; lib/barcode/scan-cache.ts:28-34; lib/barcode/resolve-scan.ts:47. Unlike the eligible-set code, there is no rules-epoch stamp on the cached policy.
confirmed.fix: Stamp the cached policy with the rules epoch and use it only when the epoch is unchanged; otherwise fall back to 'unverified'. Or re-run evaluatePolicy on-device from cached allergen tags and the current profile.
votes:
confirmed: The stale replay is real, but the finding overstates its impact.

What holds:
- `offlineMatch` (lib/barcode/client.ts:171) returns `cached.policy` as stored. `resolveOffline` (lib/barcode/scan-cache.ts) only checks age against the 30-day retention.
- I found no rules-epoch stamp or re-evaluation anywhere in the barcode path (lib/barcode/*, components/ScanConfirmSheet.tsx).
- The earlier audit's fix for item #64 (docs/audit/2026-09-13/report.md:740) made the cache store the verdict. It did not make it refreshable.
- No owner ruling or earlier audit accepts staleness for this path, as far as I could find. The only offline-barcode rulings and audits I found are #64 and the P9 account-handle reviews, which cover other issues.
- So an allergen or Avoid mark added after the original scan will not show on an offline rescan of the same product within 30 days.

What the finding gets wrong:
- It says the offline commit "never gets a server `flagged` mark". The queued commit replays to the server on reconnect. `/api/log/commit` re-evaluates against current rules (lib/server/log-commit-policy.test.ts), and `lib/log-commit-settle.ts:56-58` surfaces `flagged` items.
- Under the 2026-09-14 ruling "logging marks, never refuses", the offline warning is advisory in any case.
- The harm is therefore a delayed warning and a possibly misleading "allowed" at the confirm sheet, not a missed conflict. That is medium, not high.

confirmed: Confirmed by code trace; I did not run a repro. resolveScan (lib/barcode/resolve-scan.ts) caches every resolved match through toCachedRevision, which stores match.policy and allergenTags. On ScanUnavailable it calls resolveOffline, which gates only on SCAN_CACHE_RETENTION_DAYS = 30 and checks no rules epoch. offlineMatch (lib/barcode/client.ts:171) returns `policy: cached.policy ?? {verdict:"unverified"}` and `allergenTags: cached.allergen_tags`. Nothing re-evaluates the verdict against current allergens, Avoid marks or conditions. The confirm UI reads match.policy directly: BarcodeDraftEditor.tsx:68-71 and SanityNotices take only the blocked or unverified branches, so a stale "allowed" shows no warning. The doc comment on offlineMatch says this replay is deliberate, so it is a known trade-off with no matching owner ruling. A grep of docs/decisions and docs/audit/2026-10* found no ruling that accepts a stale cached verdict. The rules-epoch stamp from the eligible-set code is not used in lib/barcode. Severity is medium, not high. Per the 2026-09-14 ruling, logging marks and never refuses, so the failure is a missing warning and a missing server `flagged` mark. It is not a blocked write. It also needs the user to rescan a cached product while offline, after a rules change, within 30 days.

confirmed.title: Duplicate-capture 409 shows an unrelated or empty draft
confirmed.defect: On a 409 duplicate_request (the same input hash succeeded in the last 10 minutes) settle() calls latestDraft(), which returns the most recently saved localStorage draft of any capture, regardless of method, hash or age. The draft is cleared on commit, so there is usually none; if some other abandoned draft exists, it is shown.
confirmed.failureScenario: User logs 'black coffee' by text, commits it (draft cleared), and logs the same text for the same slot again within 10 minutes. The server returns 409, latestDraft() is null, and the sheet shows 'You just sent this. Here it is again.' with no draft, a dead end. If an unrelated earlier unsaved draft is still in localStorage (app killed, never dismissed), that draft is presented as the result and can be saved as the wrong food.
confirmed.evidence: components/CaptureSheet.tsx:270-273; lib/capture/drafts.ts latestDraft (any key with the prefix, newest savedAt); lib/server/capture.ts assertNotDuplicate (ok ai_calls with same hash in 10 min).
confirmed.fix: Store the draft keyed by input hash or request id and return the matching one on a 409. Or have the server return the draft, and exempt committed inputs from the duplicate guard.
votes:
confirmed: The code matches the finding, but the impact is smaller than described.

- `settle()` in components/CaptureSheet.tsx (lines 270-273) handles a `duplicate` outcome by calling `latestDraft()`.
- `latestDraft()` in lib/capture/drafts.ts scans every `draft:` key for the bound account and returns the one with the newest `savedAt`. It does not filter by method, input hash or draftId.
- `assertNotDuplicate` in lib/server/capture.ts returns 409 whenever an ok `ai_calls` row has the same input hash within 10 minutes. It does not check that the draft is still open.
- A draft is cleared on commit (line 293) and on dismiss (line 346). After a commit, a repeat of the same input therefore gets 409 with no matching draft.

The draft is only unrelated or missing in two cases:
- **No draft held:** with no draft in storage, the code falls through to `setMessage`. The user sees "You just sent this. Here it is again." with nothing shown. The typed text stays in the box and they can edit it, so this is a misleading message, not a hard dead end.
- **Stale draft held:** an abandoned draft from an app kill survives in storage. It is shown in place of the current request, and the user could save it as the wrong food. This needs a leftover draft, so it is rare.

I found no guard in the code and no test or owner ruling that accepts this behaviour. The tests only cover the server 409.

confirmed: Confirmed by code trace; I did not run it. A 409 becomes `{kind:"duplicate"}` in lib/capture-client.ts:81, with the copy "You just sent this. Here it is again." The duplicate branch in `settle()` (components/CaptureSheet.tsx:270-273) calls `latestDraft()` with no draft id, method, hash or age check. `latestDraft()` (lib/capture/drafts.ts:87-100) returns the newest-`savedAt` draft under the account prefix, whatever capture it came from. Two outcomes follow. (1) Commit success runs `clearDraft(draft.draftId)` in `save()`. A repeat of the same input then finds no draft. `held` is null, so the code only calls `setMessage("You just sent this. Here it is again.")` and shows nothing to "see again". The message is misleading, but the text box stays, so the user is not fully stuck. (2) If an abandoned draft from another capture is still in localStorage (app killed, never dismissed), `setDraft(held)` shows that unrelated draft under the duplicate message. Saving it would log the wrong food. The server probe (`assertNotDuplicate` in lib/server/capture.ts) matches `ok` ai_calls with the same input hash in 10 minutes, so it does fire on a repeat after a commit. I found no owner ruling that accepts this. Impact is a misleading message, or an unrelated draft shown, so low severity.

confirmed.title: Offline or queued log commits skip the server policy marks and the commit's other server work
confirmed.defect: A commit that gets a 5xx, 408, 429, 401 or network failure is queued as a log_entries op and applied by POST /api/sync/ops, which calls apply_sync_op directly. It never goes through applyLogEntry. The only source of `flagged` (blocked, unverified-allergen and Avoid marks), recordFingerprint, deleteCommittedMedia and the stale_revision check is applyLogEntry. The comment in queue-commit.ts says both paths reach applyLogEntry, which is false.
confirmed.failureScenario: Offline, or on a 5xx, a user logs a food on her Avoid list or containing a listed allergen via search, capture or scan. The op drains through /api/sync/ops. The card never gets the flags, `unverified:allergen` / 'Check the label' marks never appear, and no rules-unreadable notice appears. The 'logging marks, never refuses' ruling is only honoured on the online path. Draft media from a queued capture is also not deleted at commit, so it waits for the 24 h sweep.
confirmed.evidence: app/api/sync/ops/route.ts (applyOp calls rpc apply_sync_op only, then stamps occasions); lib/log/queue-commit.ts:64-79; lib/log-commit-settle.ts:56-60 sets flags only from result.flagged.
confirmed.fix: Re-evaluate policy after a drained log_entries op applies, for example by calling a policyIssues-style check from sync/ops or reading flags on the post-sync reconcile. Or route queued log creates through applyLogEntry.
votes:
confirmed: The mechanism holds. safeQueue/queue (lib/log/queue-commit.ts) enqueues a log_entries op. The drain goes through POST /api/sync/ops, which applyOp sends straight to the apply_sync_op RPC. That route only stamps the occasion afterwards. The `flagged` marks, recordFingerprint, deleteCommittedMedia and staleRevision are only in applyLogEntry (lib/server/log.ts ~259-308). The sync route never calls it. The comment "Both paths reach applyLogEntry" is false. The only place `flagged` is applied to a card is reconcileEntry, which reads result.flagged from the online response (lib/log-commit-settle.ts:56). Nothing re-judges an entry after the drain. Draft media from a queued capture is left for the 24 h sweep (the log.ts comment names the sweep as the backstop). No ruling accepts this. The 2026-09-14 ruling covers refuse versus mark on the online path, not offline parity.

Two qualifiers lower the severity. The entry is still recorded, because the ruling's core is "never refuse", and the picker adds client-side off-plan flags to the local card at pick time. So the loss is the server's authoritative marks (Avoid, allergen unverified) on queued commits, which makes it a parity gap and not data loss. The media leftover is cleaned up by the sweep. I rate it low to medium. The false comment is a certain doc bug.

confirmed: I traced this in code and did not run a repro. A queued commit is written by `queue()` in lib/log/queue-commit.ts as a `log_entries` op in the outbox. `/api/sync/ops` applies it through `applyOp`, which calls only `client.rpc("apply_sync_op")` for every entity except `food_membership`. The only post-processing is `stampLogOccasionsSafely`, and that runs only for ops with status "applied". `applyLogEntry` is not called on that route. A grep of lib and app finds `applyLogEntry` only in lib/server/log.ts and its tests. `flagged` is read only from the commit result: lib/log-commit-settle.ts:56 and lib/log/outcome.ts:33. The ops route returns no `flagged` field, so an offline or drained commit never gets the server's blocked, Avoid or unverified-allergen marks. It also gets no rules-unreadable notice. `recordFingerprint` and `deleteCommittedMedia` live in the `applyLogEntry` path, so they are skipped too, and capture draft media waits for the 24 h sweep. The comment at queue-commit.ts line 49, "Both paths reach applyLogEntry", is false. I found no owner ruling that accepts this. The 2026-09-14 "logging marks, never refuses" ruling does not mention the offline path. Client-side flags from add time (`LoggedFood.flags`) may still show on the card, so the impact is limited to the server-derived marks. I rate it medium.

confirmed.title: Capture sheet refuses to save blocked items, contradicting the logging-marks ruling
confirmed.defect: canSave returns false when any kept item has policy.verdict 'blocked', and commitDraft returns invalid 'nothing to save' without any network call. The 2026-09-14 ruling says logging marks and never refuses, because the diary must record what was eaten, and changed only the server. The photo, voice, text and label capture path still prevents saving a blocked item.
confirmed.failureScenario: User with gluten on her avoid list photographs a plate that includes bread and wants to record it. The bread item is blocked, so Save is disabled and commitDraft refuses. She must delete the bread to log the meal, so the diary lacks the item that explains a later flare. This is the exact case the ruling was made to prevent.
confirmed.evidence: lib/capture-client.ts:298-301 `kept.every((item) => item.policy.verdict !== 'blocked' && item.foodRefId !== null)` and commitDraft's early return; CaptureDraftEditor `ready = canSave(items)`; docs/decisions/2026-09-14-logging-marks-never-refuses.md ('Refusing to write something down does not stop it having been eaten').
confirmed.fix: Let blocked items be saved with a visible mark, with confirmation if wanted, and keep only the ungrounded (no foodRefId) condition as a hard stop.
confirmed.knownBefore: Partly known. docs/audit/2026-09-14-loop010/README.md raised the refuse-or-mark question and the 2026-09-14 ruling answered it for the server. No audit or ruling mentions the capture sheet's client-side canSave refusal.
votes:
confirmed: The code is as described. `canSave` in lib/capture-client.ts:296-300 returns false when any kept item has `policy.verdict === "blocked"`. `commitDraft` (line 363) returns invalid "nothing to save" before any network call. `CaptureDraftEditor` line 169 uses `canSave` for its Save button, and it also forces `blocked` onto items named in `blockedItemIds`. The comment cites "Spec AC9: a blocked item never leaves this sheet", which is the pre-ruling W3-10 behaviour.

Nothing refutes it. The 2026-09-14 ruling (docs/decisions/2026-09-14-logging-marks-never-refuses.md) only names the server commit and says what changes "is only what the server does", so it did not change the client.

The ruling's reasoning applies directly to capture: a diary should record what was eaten, and "Refusing to write something down does not stop it having been eaten." The project already reads the ruling more widely. features.md F-119 says the coach applies a blocked food, marked, "(ruling 2026-09-14)". Capture is the one log path that still refuses. lib/plan/photo-log.ts repeats the stale AC9 rule.

Mitigations leave this at medium. A manual "Log a food" search still logs with a flag, so she can record the bread another way, and the safety verdict itself is not weakened. The capture sheet still contradicts the ruling's intent.

I did not run any tests.

confirmed: Reproduced by reading the real call path. In lib/capture-client.ts, canSave (lines 296-300) returns false if any kept item has policy.verdict "blocked". commitDraft (lines 359-365) calls canSave on the edited items and returns {status:"invalid", issues:[{message:"nothing to save"}]} before any network call. CaptureDraftEditor.tsx:169 uses `ready = canSave(items) && ...`, so the Save button is disabled as well. The only way past it is to remove the blocked item, because a swap resets the policy to "unverified". Tests tests/client/capture-client.test.ts lines 231-232 and 314-320 pin this behaviour as "Spec AC9: a blocked item never leaves this sheet".

The 2026-09-14 ruling (docs/decisions/2026-09-14-logging-marks-never-refuses.md) says logging marks and never refuses, because a diary that refuses to record a blocked food is wrong exactly where it matters. It changed only /api/log/commit and does not mention the capture sheet. The server already returns `flagged` for blocked items, so the client-side refusal now contradicts it.

The ruling does not explicitly accept the capture-sheet refusal, so I treat it as a real spec mismatch rather than accepted behaviour. The severity is medium. It is a deliberate, tested pre-ruling spec (AC9) that has not been reconciled with the ruling, and the user can still log the meal without the blocked item.

confirmed.title: Barcode scan stores qty and 'g' unit inconsistent with grams
confirmed.defect: For the '100 g' pill (portionId null) the editor computes grams = (explicitGrams ?? 100) x qty, but ScanConfirmSheet builds the item with unit 'g' and qty = edits.qty (the 'How many' stepper). The optimistic card (catalogCard) uses qty = grams for unit g, so the card and the stored row disagree.
confirmed.failureScenario: Scan a product, choose the '100 g' pill and set How many = 3. grams = 300 and the snapshot is for 300 g, but the log_item is stored qty 3, unit 'g', grams 300. The export (lib/server/export.ts) prints qty 3 / unit g / grams 300. The entry fingerprint and any consumer reading qty with unit 'g' see 3 g. The coach day-context formats `${qty} ${unit}`.
confirmed.evidence: components/ScanConfirmSheet.tsx:55 `unit: edits.portionId === null ? 'g' : 'portion', portionId: edits.portionId` with `qty: edits.qty`; components/coach/editors/BarcodeDraftEditor.tsx:60 gramsFor; lib/log/catalog-card.ts `qty: portion ? qty : grams`.
confirmed.fix: When portionId is null send qty = grams with unit 'g', as catalogCard and the Log sheet do.
votes: confirmed: Confirmed by reading the code; I ran nothing. For the '100 g' pill, components/ScanConfirmSheet.tsx:55 stores unit 'g' with qty = edits.qty (the "How many" stepper), while gramsFor in BarcodeDraftEditor.tsx computes grams = (explicitGrams ?? 100) × qty. The repo convention is that unit 'g' means qty equals grams: gramsFromUnit in lib/log/grams.ts, catalogCard in lib/log/catalog-card.ts, and lib/log/deferred-refresh.ts. lib/log/contract.ts has no consistency check, so the row is accepted. It also fires at qty 1: a product with no portions defaults to the 100 g pill and stores qty 1 / grams 100, and 'Use typical serving' stores qty 1 / grams 150. The optimistic card shows qty = grams, but the server row replaces it on sync (lib/log/card-items.ts). Impact is limited because the nutrition snapshot uses grams and stays correct. Downstream consumers that read qty with unit 'g' (export, coach day-context line) see wrong amounts; I did not run those paths. I found no ruling or audit that accepts this.
