confirmed: I traced this through the code and did not run it. components/ScanConfirmSheet.tsx:55 builds the item as `grams: edits.grams, qty: edits.qty, unit: portionId === null ? "g" : "portion"`. In BarcodeDraftEditor, `gramsFor` returns `(explicitGrams ?? 100) * qty` when portionId is null. With the 100 g pill and How many = 3, the request therefore carries qty 3, unit "g", grams 300. The optimistic card uses `qty: portion ? qty : grams` (lib/log/catalog-card.ts), so it shows qty 300 for the same entry. The search path (LogFoodSheet.tsx:358) sends `qty: entry.qty`, which is grams for unit g, so it stores qty 300. The scan path is the odd one out. The 100 g pill with an explicit serving of 45 g has the same fault: qty 1, unit "g", grams 45. The stored row is `log_items.qty` 3 with unit "g", and lib/server/export.ts:225 writes `qty: Number(item.qty)` and `unit: item.unit` unchanged. The macro snapshot is built from grams, so calories and macros are correct. The damage is limited to qty/unit consistency: anything that reads qty together with unit "g" sees 3 g instead of 300 g. A fix would send `qty: grams` when portionId is null. I found no owner ruling that accepts the current behaviour. Severity is low to medium because the nutrition totals are unaffected.

confirmed.title: Label food rows are created before the request is validated, so refused or retried commits leave orphans
confirmed.defect: applyLogEntry calls commitLabelFood (inserts a user_foods row and a food_ref) before unknownRefIssues, staleRevision and the apply_sync_op RPC. If any of those refuse or the RPC throws, the entry does not exist, so existingLabelRef finds nothing on the retry and a second user_foods row is inserted.
confirmed.failureScenario: A label meal (the label item plus a catalog item pinned to a revision that has since been superseded) gets stale_revision. The label food was already inserted. Each retry or re-pick inserts another 'label_scan' food with the same name, so the user's own-foods list fills with duplicates. The same happens when apply_sync_op returns a 5xx and the client retries.
confirmed.evidence: lib/server/log.ts:275-286 (commitLabelFood precedes unknownRefIssues, staleRevision and rpc); lib/server/log-label-food.ts:133-141 (existingLabelRef returns null when the entry does not exist yet).
confirmed.fix: Run the ref and revision validation first, or make the label food creation idempotent, for example keyed by draft_id.
votes: confirmed: The ordering is as described. In lib/server/log.ts, applyLogEntry calls commitLabelFood (lines 275-276) before unknownRefIssues, staleRevision and the apply_sync_op RPC. commitLabelFood calls existingLabelRef, which looks up the log_entries row. That row does not exist until the RPC applies, so saveLabelFood inserts a user_foods row (kind label_scan) and a food_ref every time. I found no compensating cleanup and no name-based dedupe. A stale_revision refusal, an unknown-ref refusal or an RPC throw therefore leaves an orphan, and each retry adds another. Impact is small, so low is the right severity. Nothing lists user_foods in the UI. The only reader is searchExactUserFood in lib/server/coach-ports.ts, an exact-name lookup that takes one row (limit 1), so duplicates with identical label data are harmless. The Foods tab reads the local store, and the "own-foods list fills with duplicates" claim is overstated. The 2026-09-13 audit (findings-full.json) judged a similar duplicate-insert path in the same code as an invisible, inert orphan row and a hygiene gap, and it set the severity there. No owner ruling accepts the behaviour. The residual cost is slowly accumulating orphan rows.

confirmed: I confirmed this by reading the code. I did not run a repro.

In `applyLogEntry` (`lib/server/log.ts`), `commitLabelFood` runs before `unknownRefIssues`, `staleRevision` and the `apply_sync_op` RPC. `saveLabelFood` (`lib/server/log-label-food.ts`) does an unconditional `user_foods` insert with `kind: "label_scan"`, then calls `get_or_create_food_ref`. Nothing deduplicates by name or content.

The only retry guard is `existingLabelRef`. It returns null unless a `log_entries` row for `entry_id` already exists. Any refusal after the insert (`unknownRefIssues`, `stale_revision`) or an RPC error that throws leaves no entry. A retry with the same `entry_id` therefore inserts another `user_foods` row and food_ref with the same name.

The stale-revision scenario works as described. A label item plus a catalog item pinned to a superseded revision makes `staleRevision` return a refusal after the label food is saved. The same happens on a 5xx from `apply_sync_op`.

I found no owner ruling that accepts this behaviour. The only mention of the ordering is a code comment saying the swap must happen before `unknownRefIssues`.

Impact is orphan clutter and duplicate rows in the user's own-foods list. There is no safety or number error, so low severity is right.

confirmed.title: Undo of a deleted entry drops the meal title
confirmed.defect: undoDeleteEntry rebuilds the commit with buildCommitRequest but passes no `title`, so the restored server entry has title null. confirmed.failureScenario: User saved a meal named 'Post-gym lunch' with 3 items. The coach deletes it and the user taps Undo. The new entry carries no title, and after the next pull, or on another device, the card reads the derived title instead of 'Post-gym lunch'.
confirmed.evidence: lib/coach/apply-entries.ts:138-150 (no title, portionId null); lib/log/reconcile.ts:100-107 (title null derives a name); lib/log-client.ts:88-92.

votes:
confirmed: I read the code and found no guard or ruling that prevents this. undoDeleteEntry (lib/coach/apply-entries.ts:136-150) calls buildCommitRequest with no title. buildCommitRequest (lib/log-client.ts:91-92) then sends no title, so the restored entry has title null. confirmed: Traced by code reading; I did not run a repro. undoDeleteEntry (lib/coach/apply-entries.ts:136-147) calls buildCommitRequest with no `title`. buildCommitRequest (lib/log-client.ts:91-92) sets req.title only when args.title is null or a non-empty string, so the request carries no title key. The user's custom name 'Post-gym lunch' is therefore replaced by a derived name on the next reconcile or pull, and other devices never see it. The local addExtra card keeps entry.name only until then. Restored items also pass portionId: null and set no was_edited flag. The loss is real but limited to a display title and portion metadata, so severity stays low.

confirmed.title: Re-Favor of a family is a silent no-op for a ref minted after the first Favor
confirmed.defect: favor_food_families treats a family whose membership row already has status 'eats' as already favored and writes nothing. The same migration changes get_or_create_food_ref so a ref minted after a Favor does not inherit 'eats' (line 251, favor_rev = rev). A family can therefore be 'eats' while some of its current refs have no 'eats' pref. A second Favor skips those refs, and planFavor still reports the family as favorable.
confirmed.failureScenario: The user favors 'kiwi' (refs A and B written, favor_rev = rev). Later a new catalog ref C for the kiwi family is minted and does not inherit 'eats'. C becomes an 'Eaten often' item. GET /api/foods/taste returns favorable:true because the family verdict is 'eats' and every member is allowed. The user taps Favor. The RPC finds v_status = 'eats', adds the family to v_favored, writes no user_food_prefs rows and returns status ok. The client shows 'Added to your usual foods', but C is still not Favored. The row keeps offering Favor, and every tap repeats the no-op. The test 'a ref minted after a Favor does not inherit eats' only covers a later ordinary mark, not a second Favor.
confirmed.evidence: 20261215090000_favor_food_families.sql:162 `if v_status = 'eats' then v_favored := v_favored || v_name; else v_write := v_write || v_name;`; line 251 skips the backfill when `v_status = 'eats' and v_favor_rev is not distinct from v_rev`; lib/server/taste-favor.ts:152 `marks.get(family)?.status === "eats" ? "eats" : "ok"` makes this family favorable.
confirmed.fix: In the preflight, treat a family as already favored only if every ref in the captured set already has an 'eats' pref. Otherwise write the prefs for the missing refs, keeping the membership rev and favor_rev as they are or bumping them. Make planFavor's 'eats' verdict and `favorable` depend on the same per-ref check.
votes:
confirmed: I read the code and found no guard and no ruling that accepts this.

The SQL matches the finding:
- In `favor_food_families` (supabase/migrations/20261215090000_favor_food_families.sql, around line 162), a family whose membership status is already 'eats' goes into `v_favored`. It does not go into `v_write`. No `user_food_prefs` rows are written for it.
- The write loop only covers `v_write`.
- `get_or_create_food_ref` skips the 'eats' backfill when `favor_rev = rev`. A ref minted after a Favor therefore has no 'eats' pref.
- The preflight only checks that the family's current ref set equals the captured set, so a new ref C does not block the call.

The TypeScript side agrees:
- `planFavor` in lib/server/taste-favor.ts gives a family the verdict "eats" when the mark is 'eats' and every member is allowed. `favorable` is true for "ok" or "eats".
- `favorTasteKey` sends "eats" families to the RPC. The RPC returns ok with `favored` containing the family and `written` empty. The client then reports success.
- The spec (docs/specs/phase-18-open-world-foods.md, line 862) states that "already eats" families count as favorable, so this is not a documented exception.

I did not run the SQL or a vitest file; this is from reading the code. I also found no mechanism that repairs the missing pref other than an ordinary membership write.

Severity is lower than medium. Nothing is corrupted and no rule is bypassed. The ref only misses the Favored boost, and an ordinary Eats/Favored mark on that family fixes it. If C resolves to the same taste key as A or B, `history.favored` already contains the key and the button is hidden, so the loop is narrower than the finding says.

confirmed: I traced this by reading the code. I did not run SQL or write a repro. The first Favor writes membership 'eats' with favor_rev = rev. get_or_create_food_ref (migration lines ~249-253) then skips the backfill for a ref minted later. The repo's own test at tests/migrations/favor-families-db.test.ts:122 asserts that a later ref, "Kiwi, baby", ends up with no pref ('none'). Planning treats the family as favorable: planFavor (lib/server/taste-favor.ts:152) gives the family verdict "eats" whenever the membership status is 'eats' and every member is allowed. The new ref's family set includes the ref, and a ref with no pref is not an avoid. The favorable flag stays true, and favorTasteKey sends the family to the RPC. In favor_food_families (line 162), `if v_status = 'eats' then v_favored := v_favored || v_name` only appends the name to v_favored and never writes. The RPC returns status 'ok' with favored=[kiwi], and favorTasteKey maps that to favored:true. The new ref still has no 'eats' pref, and no test covers a second Favor. confirmed.title: Phone membership cache makes a repeat tap a no-op after a server-side Favor or a mark from another device
confirmed.defect: setFoodMembership decides 'unchanged' from the device-local membership cache (readFoodMembership, localStorage). The cache is written only by this device's own marks. Nothing updates it from a sync pull or from POST /api/foods/favor, which writes the server membership row and prefs directly. When the cache holds {status:null} or the same status as the requested one but the server now differs, the call returns without queuing an op.
confirmed.failureScenario: The user clears 'Kiwi', so the cache holds {status:null, rev:R}. They then tap Favor on 'Kiwi' in Eaten often. The server sets membership 'eats' and the next sync projects it. The cache still says null. In Foods the user taps to remove Kiwi from Favored, calling setFoodMembership('Kiwi', null). `previous?.status === status` is true (null === null), so the function returns null and queues no op. The local row goes neutral, but the server stays 'eats'. The next pull restores Favored and the removal is lost. The same happens when another device set the mark.
confirmed.evidence: lib/foods/prefs-client.ts:330-338 `const previous = readFoodMembership(userId, nameNorm); const unchanged = !olderActive && previous?.status === status && previous.note === note; if (unchanged) { ...; return null; }`. rememberMembership is called only at lines 354, 494 and 528 and from reconcileFoodMembership (a rejected-op revert). The Favor client (lib/foods/favor-client.ts) does not touch the cache.
confirmed.fix: Update the cache on a pull of user_food_prefs and on a successful favor. Alternatively drop the 'unchanged' shortcut unless the cache entry was confirmed by a server answer, or compare against the live local food row.
votes: confirmed: The mechanism holds in the code. `commitFoodMembership` (lib/foods/prefs-client.ts:330-338) returns null without queuing an op when `readFoodMembership` matches the requested status and note. The membership cache lives in localStorage under FOOD_PREF_REFS_KEY. Only lib/foods/prefs-client.ts reads or writes that key. `rememberMembership` is called only from `commitFoodMembership` after an enqueue (line 354), `setFoodMembershipGuarded` (494), `repairFoodMembershipCache` (528) and `reconcileFoodMembership` (a rejected-op revert). The sync pull in lib/sync/client.ts does not touch the cache. lib/foods/favor-client.ts only POSTs and leaves the cache alone. The callers in components/MyFoods.tsx (`saved` and the move handler) call `setFoodMembership` with no server-side check first, so nothing guards the no-op. The cache has to hold an entry first, which needs an earlier local mark of the same food. A food never marked on this device has `previous === undefined`, so the call goes through. That makes the failure narrower than the finding suggests, but a user who cleared Kiwi, then used Favor, then removed it matches the scenario. I did not run a repro and found no owner ruling that accepts this. The mark that gets dropped is the user's removal; the rest of the finding (Favored restored by the next pull) follows from the server row staying 'eats'. Medium severity is fair, perhaps low-medium.

confirmed: Confirmed by code trace; I did not run a repro. In lib/foods/prefs-client.ts, commitFoodMembership (lines ~330-338) returns null without queuing an op when `!olderActive && previous?.status === status && previous.note === note`. `previous` comes from readFoodMembership, which reads only the localStorage key "meal-companion:food-pref-refs". rememberMembership, the only writer of the membership entries, is called only at lines 354 (own mark), 494 (guarded mark), 528 (repairFoodMembershipCache) and from reconcileFoodMembership, which runs on a rejected-op revert. A grep of lib, components and app shows no other writer of FOOD_PREF_REFS_KEY, and no sync-pull or applyServer path touches the membership cache. lib/foods/favor-client.ts only POSTs and does not update it. So after a clear (cache {status:null, rev:R}) and a server-side Favor or another device's mark, the cache stays {null}. A later setFoodMembership(name, null) hits the no-op branch and queues nothing. The server stays 'eats' and the next pull restores Favored. Conditions are narrow: the cache must hold an entry (an undefined entry never matches) that equals the requested status. That fits the clear-then-Favor and cross-device cases in the finding. The UI callers (components/MyFoods.tsx:302 and :381) go straight to setFoodMembership, so nothing else guards this.

confirmed.title: An unreadable or over-long document amount silently becomes one household portion
confirmed.defect: cleanAmount returns null both when no amount is written and when an amount is written but fails its screen (over 24 characters, over 4 words, or no digit). parseAmount(null) then returns {count:1} ('one household portion, the set_slot_meal default'). So an amount that was present but cut by the screen is placed as a default single portion, with no 'Couldn't read the amount' message.
confirmed.failureScenario: A plan line '3 large eggs (about 150 g)' (6 words) or '1 1/2 cups (about 360 ml)' (25 characters) or '200 g cooked weight, drained' is cleaned to null, then parsed as {count:1}. The foods are grounded as one usual portion (one egg, 1 cup or similar) instead of 3 eggs or 200 g. The meal is shown and placed with confident but understated calories and protein. I reproduced this with tsx: all three inputs gave amount null and parseAmount {count:1}.
confirmed.evidence: lib/plan/document-clean.ts cleanAmount (lines 17-23) returns null on `text.length > 24 || text.split(" ").length > 4`. lib/plan/document-clean.ts parseAmount: `if (!amount) return { count: 1 }`. lib/plan/document-ground.ts:71 only leaves a food out when parseAmount returns null, which never happens for a null amount.
confirmed.fix: Have cleanFoods keep whether the model gave an amount. Pass a distinct 'unreadable' state for a screened-out amount so groundFood leaves the food out ('Couldn't read the amount'). Or extract the leading quantity and unit from long amounts before applying the length cap.
votes:
confirmed: The code matches the finding.

- cleanAmount (lib/plan/document-clean.ts:17-23) returns null in two cases: when no amount was written, and when a written amount fails the screen (over 24 characters, over 4 words, or no digit).
- parseAmount (line 158) maps a null amount to {count:1}, so both cases become one household portion.
- groundFood (lib/plan/document-ground.ts:84) only reports "Couldn't read the amount" when parseAmount returns null, which cannot happen for a null input.
- The model schema (lib/ai/document.ts) allows amounts up to 40 characters and tells the model to copy them as written. Strings like "1 1/2 cups (about 360 ml)" or "200 g cooked weight, drained" therefore reach the screen and get cut.
- The existing test (tests/plan/document-files.test.ts:56-66) only checks cleanAmount and parseAmount separately. It does not check the combined path, and it does not decide that a rejected amount should read as one portion.
- I found no owner ruling in docs/decisions or docs/audit that accepts this.

Severity is medium, not high. Nothing is written without the user's confirmation: a meal plan's meal is grounded and shown for review, and placed through set_slot_meal only after "Use for this meal". The result is a wrong default portion with no warning, not silent data corruption.

confirmed: Traced the real code path in lib/plan/document-clean.ts and lib/plan/document-ground.ts. I did not run a snippet, and I found no owner ruling that accepts this behaviour. cleanAmount strips punctuation, so parentheses are removed. It returns null for any written amount with more than 24 characters, more than 4 words, or no digit. That is the same value it returns for "no amount written". cleanFoods stores the result as DocumentFood.amount. parseAmount(null) returns {count:1} (line 158-159), not null. groundFood only leaves a food out with "Couldn't read the amount" when parseAmount returns null, and that cannot happen for a null amount. sized() then takes the first portioned hit with a count of 1 and no measure. Three inputs fail this way. "3 large eggs (about 150 g)" becomes "3 large eggs about 150 g", which is 6 words, so it cleans to null and grounds as one usual portion instead of 3 eggs. "1 1/2 cups (about 360 ml)" is over 24 characters, so it cleans to null. "200 g cooked weight, drained" is 5 words, so it cleans to null and the food is placed as one portion, not 200 g. Nothing is shown to the user, so the meal's calories and protein are understated. The model prompt (lib/ai/document.ts) asks for amounts "exactly as written" with a 40 character schema cap, which makes amounts like these likely in real documents. The screen cap is 24. The fix is to separate "no amount" from "amount present but unreadable", and to leave the food out in the second case.

confirmed.title: Starter choices ignore a wheat allergy: gluten-tagged bread is still offered
confirmed.defect: The bread starters declare only the allergen 'gluten'. starterChoices and starterExcludedByCurrentRules compare them against `allergenKey(avoid_allergens)`. 'wheat' and 'gluten' are separate keys in lib/policy/allergens.ts: 'wheat' is a major allergen and has no alias to 'gluten'. An account that avoids 'wheat' therefore keeps white bread and whole-wheat bread in its starter choices.
confirmed.failureScenario: An account with avoid_allergens ['wheat'] reaches onboarding or auto-seed. starterChoices returns white-bread and whole-wheat-bread (a vitest run printed `["wheat"] bread:true wwbread:true`). `["gluten"]` correctly removes them. The fresh-rules recheck in persistStarterSelection uses the same predicate, so it also lets them through. The user can select them as Eats and 'Pick for me' can add them. evaluatePolicy later returns 'unverified' for a wheat avoid with tags ['gluten'], so they stay out of generated plans. The user is still offered and may save a food that conflicts with their stated allergy. This contradicts the AGENTS.md rule that starters are filtered by the account's explicit dietary rules. Related: account-defined allergens such as corn or banana cannot exclude any starter, because filtering uses only each starter's declared allergen list.
confirmed.evidence: lib/foods/starter.ts:47,49 allergens:["gluten"]; lines 110 and 134 `new Set(profile.avoid_allergens.map(allergenKey))`; allergens.ts ALIASES has no wheat->gluten entry.
confirmed.fix: Tag the bread starters with both 'wheat' and 'gluten'. Make the starter check treat wheat and gluten as one concern, or reuse the policy engine's textNames/allergenRule for each starter's name.
votes: confirmed: The code defect is real. Starters white-bread and whole-wheat-bread declare allergens ["gluten"] and categories ["gluten"] (lib/foods/starter.ts:47,49). starterPassesRuleSets compares allergenKey(item allergen) against the set built from allergenKey(profile.avoid_allergens). ALIASES in lib/policy/allergens.ts has no wheat->gluten entry, and 'wheat' is a separate rule key at line 105. So an account with avoid_allergens ['wheat'] still gets both breads from starterChoices, and starterExcludedByCurrentRules (used by the fresh-rules recheck in starter-client.ts:125) lets them through too. I found no upstream guard and no owner ruling accepting this. Several things reduce the severity. The Foods picker (ALLERGEN_LABELS in lib/reference.ts) offers only 'gluten', never 'wheat'. A 'wheat' value can still be stored. normalizeAllergens accepts any string, the coach's avoidAllergens field takes any string, and the profile has an allergy_wheat synonym. Wheat is therefore reachable but not through the standard picker path. The evaluatePolicy layer, as the finding says, keeps wheat-tagged foods unverified, so they stay out of generated plans. The harm is limited to a conflicting starter being offered and saved as an Eat. The custom-allergen claim (corn, banana) is true, since filtering uses only each starter's declared allergen list. Corn-tortilla and banana declare nothing, so a custom 'corn' or 'banana' avoid does not exclude them. I did not run a test and judged this from reading the code.

confirmed: Reproduced. I ran starterChoices with an empty flags list and a profile with avoid_allergens ["wheat"], no banned categories and no avoid_food_ref_ids. It returned both white-bread and whole-wheat-bread. The same call with ["gluten"] removed both. In lib/foods/starter.ts the bread starters declare only allergens ["gluten"] and are matched through allergenKey. ALIASES in lib/policy/allergens.ts has no wheat-to-gluten entry, so "wheat" never matches. starterExcludedByCurrentRules calls the same starterPassesRuleSets predicate, so the recheck in persistStarterSelection also lets the breads through. Starters are filtered by category too, but the bread starters carry categories ["gluten"], and a wheat allergy adds no banned category. I found no decision or audit file that accepts this behaviour. The extra claim about account-defined allergens such as corn is true by construction: only each starter's declared allergens are compared, so a custom allergen can never exclude one. Severity is medium: generated plans later hold the breads back as unverified, but the starter grid still offers a food that conflicts with a stated wheat allergy. Repro file removed; no repo changes from me. An untracked tests/zz-r.test.ts appeared in the worktree and is not mine.

confirmed.title: Cured and processed meats read as 'fat' in the role inference
confirmed.defect: The PROTEIN name list has ham, prosciutto and jerky but not bacon, sausage, pepperoni, chorizo, salami, hot dog, liver or other offal. Only 'bacon fat' is matched, as pure fat. Such foods fall through to the calorie rule and, being fat-heavy, are classed 'fat'. The module header says every meat name is protein.
confirmed.failureScenario: A user adds 'Bacon', 'Pepperoni', 'Salami', 'Chorizo' or 'Hot dog'. judgeFoodRole returns {role:'fat', source:'calories'}. A vitest run gave 'Bacon', 'Pepperoni', 'Chorizo', 'Hot dog', 'Salami' and 'Liver' -> fat, while 'Ham' and 'Turkey bacon' -> protein. The Eats dot shows fat. Because the server snapshot (meal-snapshot.ts foodFor) and the phone use inferFoodRole when no role is stored, partsOf/rankPlates treat the food as a fat part and not a protein anchor. The meal generator can then pair bacon with another protein anchor, or not anchor on it.
confirmed.evidence: lib/foods/role.ts PROTEIN regex (lines 44-56) lacks bacon, sausage, pepperoni, salami, chorizo, hot dogs and offal; roleFromCalories picks fat for them.
confirmed.fix: Add bacon, sausage(s), pepperoni, salami, chorizo, hot dogs/frankfurters, liver and kidney, bratwurst and similar names to PROTEIN. Keep the 'bacon fat' PURE_FAT check ahead of it.
votes: confirmed: I ran roleFromName on 'Bacon', 'Pepperoni', 'Salami', 'Sausage', 'Hot dog' and 'Liver'. Every one returned null, so none is decided by name. The PROTEIN list in lib/foods/role.ts has no entry for any of them. The only bacon match is 'bacon fat' in PURE_FAT. These foods then fall to roleFromCalories, which classifies fat-heavy cured meats as fat; bacon's fat kcal outweighs its protein kcal several times over. The module header says every meat name is protein, so the gap is a real divergence from the stated rule. 'Ham', 'jerky' and 'prosciutto' are on the list, which makes the omission inconsistent. I found no owner ruling or test in docs/decisions or the role tests that accepts these foods as fat. I did not trace the downstream meal-generator effect of the wrong role, so the 'anchor' consequence is plausible but unverified. Severity stays low: it is a mislabelled dot and role, only when no role is stored, and it affects ranking rather than any safety verdict.

confirmed: Reproduced with tsx against lib/foods/role.ts. With bacon-like macros (37 g protein, 1.4 g carbs, 42 g fat), judgeFoodRole returned {role:'fat', source:'calories'} for Bacon, Pepperoni, Salami, Chorizo, Hot dog and Sausage. Ham returned protein by name. The PROTEIN regex has no bacon, sausage, pepperoni, salami, chorizo, hot dog or offal terms. 'bacon fat' is matched only in PURE_FAT. The calorie rule then picks fat for these fat-heavy meats, which contradicts the module header's "meat names are protein" rule. Correction: Liver was not reproduced as a general case. My run gave fat only because I fed it bacon macros. Real liver macros would usually fall to protein by calories. The core claim holds for processed and cured meats. Severity low is right: the Eats dot and role-based plate parts are misclassified, and no safety or allergy path is affected. No owner ruling accepting this was found in docs (grep for bacon in decisions and audit returned nothing). The repo is clean; my temp files were removed.

confirmed.title: Unicode fraction amounts in an uploaded meal plan are corrupted into wrong quantities
confirmed.defect: cleanAmount runs NFKC normalization before its character whitelist. NFKC turns a vulgar fraction such as ½ into '1' + U+2044 (fraction slash). U+2044 is not in the whitelist, so it is replaced by a space. The amount then reads 'N 2' instead of 'N½'. parseAmount reads that as a count of 1 or 11 household portions. The whitelist even lists ½¼¾⅓⅔, but they never survive the NFKC step.
confirmed.failureScenario: A dietitian PDF says '¾ lb chicken breast'. cleanAmount gives '3 4 lb', which parseAmount reads as 3 portions, not 340 g. '1½ cups rice' becomes '11 2 cups', which parseAmount reads as {count:11} (11 usual portions). '½ cup oats' becomes '1 2 cup', which reads as {count:1}. groundDocumentMeal then grounds these wrong gram weights, and 'Use for this meal' writes the wrong calories into the slot via set_slot_meal. I reproduced this with tsx: '½ cup' -> '1 2 cup' -> {count:1}, '1½ cups' -> '11 2 cups' -> {count:11}, '¾ lb' -> '3 4 lb' -> {count:3}. ASCII '1/2 cup' works, so only Unicode fractions are affected.
confirmed.evidence: lib/plan/document-clean.ts:16 `raw.normalize("NFKC").replace(/[^\p{L}\p{N} .,/½¼¾⅓⅔-]/gu, " ")`. parseAmount (same file) takes the leading digit run, so '11 2 cups' yields {count:11}. Consumed in lib/plan/document-ground.ts groundFood -> sized()/parseAmount.
confirmed.fix: Normalize vulgar fractions to ASCII before NFKC (½ -> 1/2, 1½ -> 1 1/2), or map U+2044 to '/', or skip NFKC for the amount and whitelist the characters directly.
votes:
confirmed: Reproduced with tsx against the checkout. cleanAmount("½ cup") returns "1 2 cup", "1½ cups" returns "11 2 cups", "¾ lb" returns "3 4 lb", and "1 ½ cups" returns "1 1 2 cups". ASCII "1/2 cup" survives. The cause is the NFKC step in lib/plan/document-clean.ts line 17 turning ½ into "1" + U+2044, which the whitelist then blanks. The whitelist's ½¼¾⅓⅔ never survive.

Nothing guards against it. cleanFoods (line 42) runs every model amount through cleanAmount before grounding. parseAmount handles Unicode fractions correctly only when it sees them, as in tests/plan/document-files.test.ts line 60, but that test bypasses cleanAmount. The model prompt in lib/ai/document.ts asks for amounts "as written", so Unicode fractions are likely in real PDFs. No owner ruling accepts this; the docs/audit and docs/decisions hits for "fraction" are unrelated.

Impact: the parsed amount is wrong (3 portions instead of 340 g for "¾ lb"; 11 portions for "1½ cups"). The wrong amount feeds the grounded calories. I downgraded severity to medium only because the "Use for this meal" step puts a confirmation between the parse and the write. The fix is small: map the vulgar fractions to ASCII, or run NFKC after protecting them.

confirmed: I reproduced this with a vitest snippet that calls the real cleanAmount and parseAmount in lib/plan/document-clean.ts. The snippet is not in the repo. Results: '½ cup' -> '1 2 cup' -> {count:1}. '1½ cups' -> '11 2 cups' -> {count:11}. '¾ lb' -> '3 4 lb' -> {count:3}. The ASCII control '1/2 cup' -> {measure:'cup', count:0.5}, so only Unicode fractions break. The cause is that line 16 runs NFKC before the whitelist. NFKC turns ½ into '1' + U+2044, and U+2044 is not in the whitelist, so it becomes a space. The fraction glyphs listed in the whitelist and in parseAmount's leadingNumber can never survive that step. The wrong amounts feed document-ground's grounding, and from there the wrong calories reach the slot. A real dietitian PDF with ½ or ¾ would hit this. I found no owner ruling that accepts the behavior. The fix is to map the vulgar fractions to ASCII (or keep them out of NFKC) before normalizing.

confirmed.title: Photo and voice capture replaces the model's total grams with qty x 100 g for 'whole' or 'piece' items that have no matching portion
confirmed.defect: gramsFor returns qty * 100 g for unit 'whole' or 'piece' whenever no catalog portion description contains that word. Most catalog portions are '1 large', '1 medium' or '1 nugget', so this default fires often. proposeDraft then uses `grams = gramsFor(...) ?? item.grams`, so the model's own visible-weight estimate is discarded. The photo prompt tells the model to give total grams and a piece count.
confirmed.failureScenario: A plate photo has 8 shrimp or 6 chicken nuggets, read as qty 8 or 6, unit piece, grams about 120. The catalog portion is '1 nugget' or '1 large'. gramsFor returns 800 g or 600 g, a 5-6x calorie overstatement in the draft. Two eggs with a 'large' portion get 200 g instead of about 100 g. The user may not catch it before commit.
confirmed.evidence: lib/capture/quantity.ts:88-90 `if ((want === "whole" || want === "piece") && Object.keys(per100g).length > 0) return qty * DEFAULT_WHOLE_GRAMS`. lib/server/capture.ts, in groundItem: `grams = gramsFor(amount.qty, amount.unit, portions, { energy_kcal: 0 }) ?? item.grams`. The per100g argument is always `{energy_kcal:0}`, so the guard is always true. Verified by tsx: gramsFor(8,'piece',[],{energy_kcal:0}) = 800.
confirmed.fix: For whole/piece with no matching portion, keep the model's item.grams (return null from gramsFor). Or use the default only when the model supplied no grams. At minimum, prefer the model estimate when it differs sharply from qty*100.
votes:
confirmed: The code matches the finding. In lib/capture/quantity.ts, gramsFor returns qty * 100 for unit 'whole' or 'piece' when no portion description contains that word. The only guard is `Object.keys(per100g).length > 0`. lib/server/capture.ts line 310 always passes `{ energy_kcal: 0 }`, so the guard is always true. The result goes through `?? item.grams`, but the 100 g default is non-null, so the model's grams are never used.

The photo prompt in lib/ai/prompts.ts asks the model for a piece count and total grams. So 8 shrimp read as qty 8, unit piece, grams about 120, with a catalog portion like '1 large', becomes 800 g.

The 100 g default is deliberate and tested (tests/capture/quantity.test.ts line 52, where 'only when per100g is known' means nutrition data exists). The test passes real nutrition data. The caller defeats that intent with a dummy value. I found no ruling in docs/decisions or docs/audit that accepts this behaviour.

The only mitigation I found is that the user reviews the draft before commit, and the draft shows a wrong amount rather than silently saving one. That keeps the severity at medium.

confirmed: Traced the real path. In lib/server/capture.ts line 310, groundItem calls `gramsFor(amount.qty, amount.unit, portions, { energy_kcal: 0 }) ?? item.grams`. The per100g argument is a literal non-empty object, so the guard `Object.keys(per100g).length > 0` in lib/capture/quantity.ts:85 is always true. For unit "whole" or "piece" with no portion whose description contains that exact word, gramsFor returns qty * 100 (DEFAULT_WHOLE_GRAMS). `??` only falls through on null, so the model's `item.grams` is never used. matchPortion matches whole words only, so descriptions like "1 large", "1 medium" and "1 nugget" do not match "piece" or "whole". The photo prompt asks the model for per-item grams (lib/ai/prompts.ts), and that estimate is discarded. The defect is real: 8 shrimp read as qty 8, unit piece, grams about 120 become 800 g. The quantity.test.ts case at line 52 shows the 100 g default was meant for a known-nutrition case, but the only caller passes a dummy per100g, so the default always fires. I did not run the snippet myself; this is code tracing plus the audit's own reported tsx result. I found no owner ruling in docs that accepts this behaviour. Severity is medium: the draft is user-reviewable before commit, but calories can be overstated 5-6x.

confirmed.title: An unparseable redirect Location in the recipe-link fetch throws a non-HttpError (500)
confirmed.defect: fetchRecipePage calls `new URL(res.location, url)` outside any try/catch. A malformed Location header (for example 'https://[') throws a TypeError. It is not an HttpError, so the route answers a generic 500 instead of the intended 422 'unreachable'.
confirmed.failureScenario: A user pastes a link whose server redirects with 'Location: http://[bad'. POST /api/plan/inspire returns an internal error instead of 'That page didn't open'.
confirmed.evidence: lib/server/recipe-url.ts:159 `if (res.location) { url = checkRecipeUrl(new URL(res.location, url).toString()); continue; }`. checkRecipeUrl handles its own parse failure, but the inner `new URL` runs first and is unguarded.
confirmed.fix: Wrap the Location resolution in try/catch and throw HttpError(422,'unreachable') on failure, or pass the raw header string to checkRecipeUrl.
votes: confirmed: At lib/server/recipe-url.ts:159, `new URL(res.location, url)` runs outside any try/catch. In Node, `new URL('http://[bad', 'https://a.com/')` throws a TypeError, which I ran to confirm. getOnce returns `res.headers.location` unvalidated. checkRecipeUrl's own try/catch only covers its own parse, which runs after the inner `new URL`. The only caller path is app/api/plan/inspire/route.ts. It wraps the call in `catch (e) { return jsonError(e) }` and nothing in between catches non-HttpErrors, so the user gets the generic error response instead of the intended 422 'unreachable'. I found no guard or owner ruling that accepts this. Impact is low: no safety or SSRF bypass, only a wrong status and message on a malicious or buggy redirect.

confirmed.title: Prepared-batch reuse picks a later row of an old batch, so the preview throws when it crosses the 2-day storage window
confirmed.defect: When planShoppingPeriod() decides whether a slot joins an existing prepared batch, chosen.find() returns the first row of the same recipe revision that passes its own check (currentDay - row.localDate <= 2). It does not look at the batch's first day. A later row of a batch that started more than 2 days earlier can match, and the new slot then takes that batch's batchId. aggregateShopping() measures against group[0] (the batch's first day), so it throws, and the SQL accept would reject it as 'batch storage window exceeded'.
confirmed.failureScenario: One person, a recipe with 4 servings that fits a slot at fraction 1, chosen on 4 consecutive days (variety 'repeat_friendly' or 'balanced'). Days 1-3 join one batch. For day 4, find() skips day 1 (3 days away) but matches day 2 (2 days away), and the servings sum 3+1=4 <= 4 passes. Day 4 gets the same batchId, and the next aggregateShopping() throws RangeError 'A prepared batch cannot cross its storage window'. The error is not an HttpError, so POST /api/shopping/preview answers 500. I reproduced it with four daily slots and one candidate recipe.
confirmed.evidence: lib/shopping/planner.ts:284-289 (prior = chosen.find(... currentDay - dayNumber(use.localDate) <= 2 ...)). lib/shopping/aggregate.ts:68-76 compares against group[0] and throws RangeError. supabase/migrations/20261128090000_recipe_plan_accept.sql batch window check (last_day - first_day > 2). Scratch run printed: 'batch THROWS: A prepared batch cannot cross its storage window'.
confirmed.fix: Judge the whole batch: find the batch's first (earliest) row and require currentDay - firstDay <= 2 (and the same shopping window) before reuse. Otherwise start a new batchId. Do the check per batchId, not per row.
votes:
confirmed: I traced the code in lib/shopping/planner.ts and lib/shopping/aggregate.ts, and the bug holds. I did not run the repro myself.

The reuse check at planner.ts:~284 is `chosen.find(...)`. It tests only `currentDay - dayNumber(use.localDate) <= 2` against each row on its own. It never compares against the first day of that row's batch.

Walk-through with a 4-serving recipe, one person, 1 serving per slot:
- Day 1 starts batch B1.
- Day 2 matches the d1 row, so it joins B1.
- Day 3 matches the d1 row (2 days away), so it joins B1.
- Day 4: `find` skips the d1 row (3 days away). It then reaches the d2 row, which is 2 days away. Its batch B1 has 3 servings used, and 3+1=4 <= 4, so the check passes. Day 4 is assigned B1.

`aggregateShopping` then groups uses by batchId. For the day-4 use it compares against `group[0]` (day 1), finds a gap of 3 days (more than 2), and throws RangeError "A prepared batch cannot cross its storage window". The planner's final `aggregateShopping` call runs on every plan, so the preview throws. A RangeError is not an HttpError, so the route returns 500.

No guard upstream stops it. The serving-sum check passes, the same-week check passes, and `keptSelectionId` is unset. I found nothing in the checked-in context that accepts this behaviour.

confirmed.title: Accept stores confirmed stock for a line whose need is unknown, because SQL LEAST ignores NULL
confirmed.defect: For new and updated lines, confirmed_stock_grams is written as least(needGrams, v_stock). In PostgreSQL, least() ignores NULL arguments. When needGrams is null (unknown raw purchase amount) and the pantry holds stock, the column gets the full pantry stock. The preview (aggregateShopping) sets confirmedStockGrams to null in that case.
confirmed.failureScenario: A recipe line has purchase_conversion_status 'unknown' and the pantry holds 200 g of that identity. The preview shows no confirmed stock, and the accept writes confirmed_stock_grams = 200 with need_grams null. The list then shows 200 g in stock against an unknown need, and what was accepted differs from what the user previewed. Related: the same update keeps checked = true when the new need is null, because the SQL comparison with null is not true, while aggregateShopping unchecks it.
confirmed.evidence: supabase/migrations/20261128090000_recipe_plan_accept.sql:577 and :584 (least((v_expected_line->>'needGrams')::numeric, v_stock)). lib/shopping/aggregate.ts:~138 sets confirmedStockGrams null when needGrams is null; the checked rule at ~167 gives false when additionalNeedGrams is null.
confirmed.fix: Use case when need is null then null else least(need, v_stock) end for both statements. Set checked = false when the old or new need is null.

PostgreSQL least() ignores NULL, so an unknown need (null) with pantry stock gets the full stock stored in shopping_lines.confirmed_stock_grams. aggregateShopping sets confirmedStockGrams to null in that case. No guard stops it: the only check constraint tying stock to need is on shopping_purchase_windows, not shopping_lines; the accept raises only in the available_quantities lock mode; 20261209090300 does not change these expressions. I found no ruling in docs/ that accepts it, though my search of docs/ was limited to a grep for confirmed_stock. The checked-flag mismatch is real as stated; I did not trace how it is displayed. I did not run the SQL. Impact is low: only the line-level stock value is wrong, and the window-level calculation handles null correctly.

confirmed: The code at lines 577 and 584 of 20261128090000_recipe_plan_accept.sql is as described, and no later migration changes it. I read the code; I did not run it against a database. Impact is limited: an unknown-need line shows stock against no need, and a checked line stays checked. buy_grams still comes out NULL.

confirmed.title: Estimator takes the median of every body_mass sample per day, which breaks the dashboard's scale-beats-manual rule
confirmed.defect: `weighInsKg` reads the raw `weigh_ins` view, which holds every body_mass sample from every source. The engine then takes the median per day (lib/expenditure.ts:271). The comment at the top of health-daily.ts says the estimator and dashboard cannot see different numbers, but the weigh-in path does not use `rollUpDay`.

With two ingest sources, or a scale plus a manual copy, the Theil-Sen slope input is a blend of the sources rather than the shown weight. A source that is added or dropped mid-window adds spurious steps to the weight trend. The estimator's weightTrendKg then disagrees with the number the user sees.

- `seriesOf` (lib/expenditure.ts:264-271) takes the median of all readings on a day.

- Scenario from the finding: the dashboard shows 80.0 kg, and the estimator uses a median of 80.2 kg.

confirmed.title: Oura callback is an unauthenticated open redirect
confirmed.defect: The callback decodes the return path from the unverified `state` query value, and `safeReturnTo` returns `url.pathname + search + hash`. The WHATWG URL parser keeps a dot-segment path such as `/.//evil.com/x` as the pathname `//evil.com/x`. `app/api/health/oura/callback/route.ts` `back()` then runs `new URL(oauthReturnTo(state, origin), origin)`, which reads `//evil.com/x` as a protocol-relative URL and moves the host to evil.com.
confirmed.failureScenario: An attacker builds `/api/health/oura/callback?error=1&state=x.<base64url('/.//evil.com/p')>` and sends it to a victim. No session is needed, because every path through `back()` decodes the state without checking it against `oauth_states`. The victim is sent a 302 to https://evil.com/p?oura=error&reason=denied from the app's own domain, which makes a convincing phishing link. A signed-in user can also reach this through POST /api/health/oura/start with `returnTo` set to `/.//evil.com`, because `safeReturnTo` accepts it.
confirmed.evidence: lib/health/oura-return.ts:2-11 `new URL(value, origin)` then `return `${url.pathname}${url.search}${url.hash}``. lib/health/oura-return.ts:13-18 `oauthReturnTo` base64url-decodes `state.split('.')[1]` with no signature check. app/api/health/oura/callback/route.ts:17 `new URL(oauthReturnTo(state, origin), origin)`. Checked with node: `new URL('/.//evil.com/x','https://app.example').pathname` is `//evil.com/x`, and `new URL('//evil.com/x','https://app.example').origin` is `https://evil.com`.
confirmed.fix: In `safeReturnTo`, reject any normalized pathname that starts with `//`, or return a value that is not re-parsed against the origin. Have `back()` apply `startsWith('/') && !startsWith('//')` to the result, and read `returnTo` only from a verified `oauth_states` row.
votes: confirmed: I reproduced it with node. `new URL('/.//evil.com/p', origin).pathname` is `//evil.com/p`. `safeReturnTo` only rejects values that start with `//`, so `/.//evil.com/p` passes. It also passes the origin check, and the returned string is the pathname plus search and hash. `back()` in app/api/health/oura/callback/route.ts then calls `new URL('//evil.com/p', origin)`, which gives `https://evil.com/p`. That is a 302 to an attacker-chosen host. `oauthReturnTo` decodes `state.split('.')[1]` without checking it against `oauth_states`. The `error=1` path and every other `back()` path therefore redirect unauthenticated. The only gates are `HEALTH_INGEST_ENABLED` and a rate limit of 20 per hour per IP. When `HEALTH_INGEST_ENABLED` is off, `back()` still redirects with reason `disabled`. The rate limit sits ahead of most `back()` calls, but if it throws, the catch block calls `back()` anyway. I did not find a middleware guard or an owner ruling that accepts this. The redirect is an open redirect: it carries no credentials, and the attacker cannot choose the query string. Medium severity fits.

confirmed: I reproduced it with tsx against the real code. A state of `x.` + base64url('/.//evil.com/p') makes `oauthReturnTo` return `//evil.com/p`, because `safeReturnTo` passes: the value does not start with `//`, and `new URL` keeps the origin and normalizes the dot-segment. In `back()` in `app/api/health/oura/callback/route.ts`, `new URL('//evil.com/p', origin)` then resolves to `https://evil.com/p?oura=error`, and `Response.redirect` sends a 302 there. The callback never checks `state` against `oauth_states` before `back()` runs. With `?error=1` it redirects at once, with no session. The redirect also happens when `HEALTH_INGEST_ENABLED` is unset (reason "disabled"). The fix is to reject a result that starts with `//` after normalization, or to check `new URL(result, origin).origin === origin`.

confirmed.title: Targets sheet dates a manual revision by the UTC day, not the phone's local day
confirmed.defect: TargetModeSheet builds effectiveFrom with new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10), which is the UTC date. Every other target writer uses the phone's local day (todayIso() / targetDayFor() in lib/settings/date.ts and lib/targets/revision.ts). lib/server/targets.ts says the server dates a revision by the day the phone sends, and authorTargets stores it as effective_from without change.
confirmed.failureScenario: A user in US Pacific time saves grams or percent targets at 6 pm local on 10 Oct. UTC is already 11 Oct, so the revision gets effective_from = 11 Oct. Per AGENTS.md, a future-dated revision waits in the history, so today keeps the old numbers and the save looks ignored until tomorrow. A user east of UTC saving in the morning gets yesterday's UTC date. That backdates the revision and rewrites the target of the day before, which is already in the past.
confirmed.evidence: components/TargetModeSheet.tsx:53 `const today = new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10);`, used at lines 58 and 61 as `effectiveFrom: today`. The sibling writers in lib/targets/revision.ts default to todayIso(), which is localIsoDate(new Date()) (lib/settings/date.ts:7). The route passes body.effectiveFrom straight through as input.today (app/api/targets/route.ts:109), and lib/server/targets.ts:354 writes `effective_from: req.effectiveFrom`.
confirmed.fix: Use todayIso() from @/lib/settings/date, or targetDayFor() from @/lib/targets/revision, instead of the toISOString slice.

Failure cases:

- East of UTC, a save in the early local morning is dated yesterday, so the revision is backdated.

Medium severity looks right. It affects the manual targets sheet only, and the result self-corrects the next day. Backdating can rewrite the target for a day that has already passed.

I did not run a test. The conclusion comes from reading the code and its callers.

confirmed.title: Storage policy lets users upload to the media bucket without a media_objects row, so the sweep and sign limits are bypassed
confirmed.defect: The `media_own_folder` policy grants `for all to authenticated` on any object under the user's own `<uid>/` folder. The server design assumes every upload goes through POST /api/media/sign, which inserts a `media_objects` row, enforces 30 signs per minute and issues the object name. A client with its own JWT can call the Storage API directly and upload objects with any name. These objects have no `media_objects` row, so the daily media-sweep never lists or deletes them. The sign limit does not apply either.
confirmed.failureScenario: A signed-in user loops direct Storage uploads of 8 MB JPEGs to `media/<uid>/<random>.jpg`. Each object is permanent, because the sweep only iterates `media_objects` rows (media-sweep route lines 71-76). Storage cost grows without limit and the sign rate limit never trips. Paths that read the object without checking for a row (transcribe, plan-inspire, plan-document, pantry-photo) will also accept such an object.
confirmed.evidence: supabase/migrations/20260920090100_phase4_media_bucket.sql:13-16 (policy for all, using and with check only on foldername[1] = uid). app/api/jobs/media-sweep/route.ts:70-78 lists only `media_objects` rows. lib/server/media.ts:57-60 inserts the row only inside `signUpload`. `assertLiveMediaObject` is called only in lib/server/capture.ts, not in the other consumers.
confirmed.fix: Remove insert and update from the authenticated policy, leaving select and delete. Uploads should go only through the service-issued signed upload URL. Optionally have the sweep also list the bucket and delete objects with no row.
votes:
confirmed: The mechanism holds. Migration 20260920090100 creates `media_own_folder` as `for all to authenticated`, checked only on the first folder segment being the user's uid. The bucket limits are 8 MB and the six MIME types. No other migration changes this policy (grep found only this one).

An authenticated client with its own JWT can therefore upload straight to `media/<uid>/<anything>.jpg`. `tests/tenancy/storage.test.ts` does exactly this as its "control" case: A uploads to her own folder with a user client and no `media_objects` row.

`signUpload` (lib/server/media.ts) is the only place that inserts a `media_objects` row, and it does so before it creates the signed upload URL. Direct uploads skip it, so they skip the sign rate limit too. `app/api/jobs/media-sweep/route.ts` selects only from `media_objects` (unattached rows older than 24 h) and calls `deleteMedia` on those paths. It never lists Storage, so objects with no row are never deleted.

I found no owner ruling or audit that accepts this. Nothing in docs/decisions or docs/audit mentions orphan objects or direct Storage uploads. The only references to the policy are the plan and spec, which describe it as an owner re-check.

Impact is bounded. Each object is capped at 8 MB and the MIME list is fixed. The user can only fill their own folder. Supabase's own API limits still apply, and it takes a signed-in account, which sign-up provides. So the result is unbounded permanent storage cost from one account, not data exposure. I did not check the claim that the transcribe, plan-inspire, plan-document and pantry-photo paths accept such objects, and it is secondary.

A fix would restrict the policy to select and delete, since uploads go through the server's signed URLs, or add a sweep that lists Storage objects and compares them to `media_objects`.

confirmed: I traced this statically and did not run it against a live Storage API. The mechanism is deterministic.

- The `media_own_folder` policy in supabase/migrations/20260920090100_phase4_media_bucket.sql:13-16 is `for all to authenticated`. Its `using` and `with check` clauses test only `bucket_id='media'` and `foldername(name)[1] = auth.uid()`. It has no link to `media_objects`.
- A signed-in user with their own JWT can therefore INSERT any object name under `<uid>/` directly through the Storage API. That never touches POST /api/media/sign, so no `media_objects` row is created and the 30-per-minute sign limit does not apply.
- No later migration changes this policy. The only other mentions are the down migration and the spec.
- app/api/jobs/media-sweep/route.ts:70-78 selects only `media_objects` rows with `deleted_at` null, `entry_id` null and an old `created_at`. Objects with no row are never listed or deleted, so they persist forever.
- No docs/audit or docs/decisions entry accepts this behaviour.

The bucket-level limits still hold: 8 MB per object and the six allowed MIME types. The abuse is therefore unbounded object count at up to 8 MB each, not unbounded object size. Medium severity is reasonable.

Math.max(1, NaN) and Math.min(50, NaN) both return NaN, so `.limit(NaN)` is sent. `?limit=2.5` passes through as 2.5. I did not run the query. The installed postgrest-js (2.117.2) `.limit()` sets the URL param with `${rows}`, so the request carries `limit=NaN` or `limit=2.5`. PostgREST rejects a non-integer limit with a 400 parse error. confirmed.title: Anchor date-variety uses a signed modulo, so every date before 2026-01-01 ranks with inflated, inverted rotation
confirmed.defect: `variety = 1 - ANCHOR_ROTATION * (((tier.indexOf(anchor) + day) % tier.length) / tier.length)` uses JS `%`. `day` is `daysSinceEpoch(date)` against ROTATION_EPOCH 2026-01-01, so it is negative for any earlier date. The remainder is then in (-n, 0], the fraction is negative, and variety lands in [1, 1.3) instead of (0.7, 1]. The sibling `rotate()` in the same file normalises negatives correctly (`((by % n) + n) % n`); this site does not.
confirmed.failureScenario: A user opens a 2025 date, for example when backfilling or browsing history. Probe with planDay on eats(eggs, yogurt, tuna, oats, toast, banana, rice, broccoli, oliveOil) and three 600 kcal slots: 2026-01-02 gives breakfast score 0.830 and 2025-12-26 gives 0.954. Scores above what any post-epoch date can produce show the multiplier exceeds 1. The rotation also runs in the opposite direction: the anchor that is penalised after the epoch is favoured before it, and tier-mates tie differently. The day-assignment search also compares repeat (0.5x) against distinct plates using these inflated scores. The result is deterministic, but it is not the documented rotation and the pre-epoch day plan differs from what the model describes.
confirmed.evidence: lib/meals/plate.ts:394 (`% tier.length` with a possibly negative `day`); lib/types.ts:374 `ROTATION_EPOCH = "2026-01-01"`; lib/rotation.ts daysSinceEpoch returns a negative number before the epoch; lib/meals/plate.ts `rotate()` handles negatives correctly. Probe output: `2025-12-26 Greek yogurt and eggs with oats 0.954` against `2026-01-02 ... 0.830`.
confirmed.fix: Normalise: `const phase = (((tier.indexOf(anchor) + day) % tier.length) + tier.length) % tier.length;` and use `phase / tier.length`.
votes:
confirmed: The bug is real in code. lib/meals/plate.ts:394 computes `((tier.indexOf(anchor) + day) % tier.length)` with JS `%`. `day` comes from `rotationOf` (plate.ts:144), which returns `daysSinceEpoch(date)` and is negative for any date before 2026-01-01. rotation.test.ts:22 confirms `daysSinceEpoch("2025-12-31")` is -1. The remainder is then in (-n, 0], so variety = 1 + 0.3*|r|/n, which is in [1, 1.3) instead of (0.7, 1]. The rotation order is reversed as well. The sibling `rotate()` at plate.ts:149-153 normalises negatives with `((by % n) + n) % n`, so the omission here is inconsistent with the file's own handling. I found no upstream guard. `rotationOf` falls back to 0 only for non-finite values. I found no owner ruling in docs/decisions or the phase-17 spec that accepts it. I did not run the probe. I checked the finding by reading the code and from JS semantics.

I rate it low rather than medium. The effect is limited to plate scoring on pre-2026 dates. Every plate in that day's ranking gets an inflated multiplier, and the rotation direction flips. Days still render complete and deterministic, so the "any date renders a complete day" rule still holds. Product use of pre-2026 dates is rare, since the app launched in late 2026 and only backfill or history browsing reaches them. Safety verdicts are not affected, because ranking never changes them. The fix is a one-line normalisation of the modulo.

confirmed: lib/meals/plate.ts:394 uses `(tier.indexOf(anchor) + day) % tier.length`. `day` comes from rotationOf(date), which is daysSinceEpoch(date) and is negative for dates before 2026-01-01. JS `%` keeps the sign of the dividend. I evaluated the formula with ANCHOR_ROTATION=0.3 (plate.ts:132) and a tier of 3. For day=-7 the multipliers are [1.1, 1, 1.2], which are all at or above 1. For day=3 they are [1, 0.9, 0.8]. So pre-epoch dates get a variety multiplier in [1, 1.3) instead of (0.7, 1], and the penalty/favour order is inverted. I did not run planDay, so the cited probe scores 0.954 and 0.830 are unverified. The sibling rotate() at plate.ts:149-152 normalises negatives with `((by % n) + n) % n`, so this site is inconsistent with it. The effect is limited to a deterministic ranking nudge for historical or backfill dates. It never touches safety verdicts, so I rate it low rather than medium.

confirmed.title: Meal count and slot clocks for any viewed date come from today's cached target, not that date's revision
confirmed.defect: When mealsPerDay is null (the default), mealCountFor reads settings.activeTargetProfile.training.kcal. That is the current cache, and plannedSlotIds (lib/plan/slot-share.ts:71), timesForLayout and resolveSlotTimes (lib/resolve.ts:89) all pass store.settings. The server already derives the count from the revision in force on each entry's own date (lib/server/log-occasion.ts:74 comment, 'a past entry's meal count is the one its own day had, never today's'; trainingKcalOn(date)). The phone does not.
confirmed.failureScenario: The account has rev1 (effective 2026-01-01, 1700 kcal) and rev2 (effective 2026-10-01, 2000 kcal), and mealsPerDay is null. On 2026-10-10 the user views 2026-09-15. resolveDay returns 4 slots (the 4-meal clocks 08:00/11:30/15:00/18:30) with day target 1700 kcal. The server's rule gives 3 slots at 08:00/12:30/18:30. I reproduced this: the 2026-09-15 view shows 4 slots at 1700 kcal. A past day gets a phantom Meal 4. Its open slots split the day four ways instead of three. Occasions and templates are chosen from the wrong clocks, so Meal 3 at 15:00 becomes a snack plate. The mismatch with the server's occasion stamps feeds history affinity. The server's day-context store has the reverse problem for a future date: with the active cache null, the count falls back to 3.
confirmed.evidence: lib/plan.ts:55-62 mealCountFor uses settings.activeTargetProfile; lib/plan/slot-share.ts:71 `slotListFor(dayType, store.settings)`; lib/resolve.ts:89 `resolveSlotTimes(dayType, store.settings)`; lib/server/log-occasion.ts:72-87 reads the date's revision.
confirmed.fix: Resolve the meal count from targetRevisionOn(settings, date).training.kcal. Pass `{ ...store.settings, activeTargetProfile: targetRevisionOn(...) }` into slotListFor and resolveSlotTimes inside plannedSlotIds, timesForLayout and ratiosFor, and into swap/skip callers.
votes:
confirmed: The phone's meal count does not follow the viewed date's target revision.

- `mealCountFor` (lib/plan.ts:55-62) reads only `settings.activeTargetProfile.training.kcal`, which is today's cache. `slotListFor`, `resolveSlotTimes` (lib/plan.ts:113), `plannedSlotIds` (lib/plan/slot-share.ts:71) and `timesForLayout` (lib/resolve.ts:89) all pass `store.settings` with no date.
- The day's targets do use the date: `resolveTargets` and `targetRevisionOn` take the date. So a past day gets the old revision's kcal but the slot count and clocks from today's revision.
- The server is date-aware. `trainingKcalOn` (lib/server/log-occasion.ts:72-87) reads the revision in force on the entry's own date, and the comment says a past entry's meal count is never today's. The phase-19 spec SQL (lines 165-190) also derives the count per date from the revision, in a query that cites `mealCountFor` (it names `lib/plan.ts:52-57`).
- `mealsPerDay` defaults to null (lib/store.ts:42).
- I found no owner ruling or audit entry in docs/decisions or docs/audit that accepts this. The only spec line on the topic (phase-17 line 193) says "count as Today derives it", which is a fidelity requirement, not a ruling to use today's cache.
- I did not run a repro. The conclusion rests on reading the code and its callers.

The failure only shows when a revision change crosses the 1800 or 2600 kcal training threshold and the account has not set a meal count. Eaten slots stay visible on those days, so the impact is a phantom open slot and wrong occasion clocks on past or future days, not data loss. I rate it low rather than medium.

confirmed: Traced the call path in the worktree. `resolveDay` takes its day target from `ratiosFor` -> `resolveTargets(dayType, settings, date)` -> `targetRevisionOn(settings, date)` (lib/targets.ts:30), so the target is the revision in force on the viewed date. The meal count is not date-aware. `plannedSlotIds(store, date, dayType)` (lib/plan/slot-share.ts:71) calls `slotListFor(dayType, store.settings)`. That calls `mealCountFor(settings)` (lib/plan.ts:55-62), which reads only `settings.mealsPerDay` and `settings.activeTargetProfile.training.kcal`, the cache for today. `timesForLayout` (lib/resolve.ts:89) calls `resolveSlotTimes(dayType, store.settings)`, which calls `mealCountFor` again (lib/plan.ts:115). `generatedPlan` (lib/resolve.ts:160-161) feeds those ids and clocks into `planMealsForDay`. The `date` argument never reaches `mealCountFor`.

With rev1 at 1700 kcal and rev2 at 2000 kcal as in the finding, the cache holds 2000 kcal, so the count is 4 (08:00/11:30/15:00/18:30). Viewing a date under rev1 gives a 1700 kcal target but 4 slots. The server's `trainingKcalOn(date)` in lib/server/log-occasion.ts:72-87 gives 3 slots at 08:00/12:30/18:30. Its comment says a past entry's meal count is the one its own day had, never today's. That is exactly the phone/server disagreement described. I read the code and did not run a repro snippet. I found no owner ruling in docs/decisions or docs/audit that accepts it (only the unrelated floor-day audit mentions meal counts). The finding's secondary claim, about the server's day-context store for a future date, I did not check.

Severity medium is right: the result is wrong and visible (a phantom Meal 4, wrong slot split, wrong occasion clocks), but it only affects `mealsPerDay = null` accounts viewing dates under an earlier revision with a different training kcal band.

confirmed.title: Ticked slot with a food-bearing followPlan snapshot plus a log filed under it reads as unticked and empty
confirmed.defect: For an eaten slot whose override is followPlan with components (a time-edit snapshot or a legacy tick) and which has its own log entry, `components` becomes [] (eatenPlanSnapshotIfUnlogged is null while planSnapshot is non-null). No base meal is generated, because fixedMacros makes the slot fixed. No estimate is built either, because undescribedEatenSlots excludes a slot that holds components. meal is therefore null. eatenAt is read only `shown ? stored.eaten[slot] : undefined`, so ResolvedSlot.eaten is false.
confirmed.failureScenario: Store with eaten['meal-3'], itemOverrides['meal-3'] = {followPlan:true, components:[Salmon], time:'19:30'} and extras:[800 kcal log with slot 'meal-3']. resolveDay gives slot meal-3 eaten:false, meal:undefined, consumed 800. The card shows an unticked empty slot even though the user ticked it. Day completion (completionFor) skips it as unplanned, so a fully eaten day can read 'partially done'. A second tap writes a new eaten mark over the existing one. The count (800) is right but the card state is wrong. Existing tests (tests/plan/eaten-shell-rule.test.ts) assert only macros and consumed, never eaten.
confirmed.evidence: lib/resolve.ts:261 planSnapshot; :263-264 components = [] when planSnapshot is set but the log suppresses it; :289 `const eatenAt = shown ? stored?.eaten?.[slotId] : undefined;`. Only the Plan panel path (app/page.tsx:732 slotLogged) rewrites the slot to the logged shell. Other log entry points with a slot id do not.
confirmed.fix: Treat an eaten slot whose snapshot is suppressed by a log like the logged-ritual case: build eatenEstimateMeal(date, slot, undefined, stored) for it, so meal is non-null and eaten stays true. Or derive eaten from stored.eaten[slot] independently of `shown`.
votes:
confirmed: I reproduced it. I used a temporary probe test, since deleted, that copies the setup of tests/plan/eaten-shell-rule.test.ts ("timedDinnerWithLog", MAJOR 4 case). The code path matches the finding. The followPlan snapshot is non-null, but eatenPlanSnapshotIfUnlogged returns null because a log is filed under the slot. That sets components to []. There is no base meal for an eaten slot. The meal ternary then hits `override.followPlan && !baseMeal && !components.length`, so meal is null. undescribedEatenSlots excludes the slot because override.components is non-empty, so no estimate is built. shown is therefore null and eatenAt is undefined, which gives eaten=false.

No guard, test or owner ruling accepts this. The existing tests assert only macros and consumed, never card.eaten. The counting is correct (800 kcal); only the card state is wrong. It needs a time-edit snapshot plus a slot-tagged log that did not come through the Plan panel's logged-shell path, so it is narrow. Low severity stands.

confirmed.title: Swap sheet offers the meal that is already on the card as the first alternative
confirmed.defect: The current meal is excluded by comparing row.id with input.currentMealId. A generated meal's id is `suggested:<date>:<slot>`, and a swapped one keeps its previous baseMealId. Composed alternatives are ids of the form `plate:<foods>`, so they never equal currentMealId. The generated plate is also usually the top-ranked plate for the slot, because the swap sheet and the layout both use rankPlates, the same date and the same target.
confirmed.failureScenario: With the starter foods and a 2100 kcal rest account, Today shows meal-1 'Egg with oatmeal'. Opening Swap for meal-1 lists 'Egg with oatmeal' as the first card, with 'Swap to this'. The same happens for all 4 slots (verified: the first alternative equals the current meal name for each). The user sees the meal they already have offered as an 'other meal'. After a swap, the new plate is offered again too.
confirmed.evidence: lib/today/swap-alternatives.ts:128 `id: \`plate:${plate.key}\``; :133 `.filter((row) => row.id !== input.currentMealId)`; components/MealSwapSheet.tsx:103,116 passes `currentMealId: slot.meal?.id` (a `suggested:` id).
confirmed.fix: Also drop a composed row whose foodIds/components equal the slot's current components (or whose visibleKey equals the current meal's). Alternatively pass the current plate key and compare plate.key.
votes: confirmed: The exclusion at swap-alternatives.ts:133 compares row.id to currentMealId. A generated meal's id is `suggested:${date}:${slot}` (layout-plan.ts:83), and MealSwapSheet.tsx:103,117 passes that as currentMealId. Composed rows have ids of the form `plate:${plate.key}`, and saved rows use `recipe:` or `saved:` ids, so none can equal a `suggested:` id and the filter never fires for a generated meal. Nothing else removes the current meal: the later dedupe compares only row ids, protein keys and visible keys among the candidates themselves. The swap sheet and the layout both call rankPlates for the same slot, date and target, so the card's own plate is usually among the top-ranked rows, which matches the report. I did not run the reproduction. I found no owner ruling in docs/decisions, docs/audit or docs/specs that accepts this behaviour. The tests I found that mention currentMealId only exercise the presentational SwapSheet.

confirmed: I reproduced this with a tsx script run against the real code. It built 10 default starter foods for a 2100 kcal day split over 4 slots with clocks, ran `planMealsForDay`, then called `swapAlternatives` with `currentMealId` set to the generated `suggested:<date>:<slot>` id. The cause is as described. Generated ids are `suggested:...` (lib/foods/layout-plan.ts:83), composed rows are `plate:<key>`, and the filter at swap-alternatives.ts:133 compares only ids, so the current plate is never removed.

Result per slot:
- meal-1: current is "Egg and greek yogurt with blueberries". The alternatives list it second.
- meal-2: current is "Tofu with brown rice and broccoli". Listed second.
- meal-3: current is "Whey protein powder with banana and almonds". Listed first.
- meal-4: current is "Tempeh with brown rice and broccoli". Listed first.

So all 4 slots offer the meal already on the card. Slots 3 and 4 show it first. In slots 1 and 2 it is second, because `planDay` picks distinct anchors and the swap sheet ranks each slot alone. The claim that it is first for all four is slightly overstated. The defect is real, at medium severity.

I found no owner ruling that accepts this. The repro left no files in the repo. The untracked `docs/architecture/` and `tests/plan/zz-*.test.ts` entries in `git status` are not mine.

confirmed.title: 'Marked not eaten' leaves the frozen generated meal in place as a hand-edit
confirmed.defect: Ticking a generated meal rewrites the slot override with the plate's components and drops followPlan. Unticking only clears the eaten mark; it never removes or restores that override. The slot stops following the plan after an Undo or untick.
confirmed.failureScenario: The user ticks Meal 2 (writes override{baseMealId:'suggested:…', title, components}, no followPlan), taps the 'marked eaten' Undo or unticks it, then later changes targets, adds a logged snack or puts a food on Avoid. The 'Back to the suggested meal' button is needed to recover. Undo of a tick does not return the day to the state before the tick. features.md calls ticking a simple eaten mark.

confirmed: Confirmed by tracing the code. I did not run a snippet. In `writeEatenSlot` (lib/plan-day-client.ts:242-249), a tick with a `generated` plate and no override, or one that still has `followPlan`, writes an override. (lib/sync/plan-days.test.ts) asserts that `followPlan` is undefined after the tick. confirmed.title: foodsFor reads all user_foods, including soft-deleted rows, with unpaged and unbatched queries on every coach turn
confirmed.defect: `foodsFor` runs `user_foods.select().eq(user_id)` with no `deleted_at` filter and no paging, so it hits the 1,000-row cap silently. It then runs `food_refs ... .in("user_food_id", ids)` with every id in one URL, and `user_food_prefs ... .in("food_ref_id", refIds)` unbatched. `userFoodRefIds` in the same file was fixed to use `fetchAllRows` and `fetchAllChunked`, but this function was not.
confirmed.failureScenario: Label scans and custom foods each create a `user_foods` row, and soft-deleted rows are never dropped from this read. An active account that accumulates a few hundred foods over months gets a very long GET URL on every coach turn (`serverStoreFor`), plan-ideas call and compose pool. The query fails with a 4xx and the coach or chip request returns an error. Past 1,000 foods the list is silently truncated, so the coach plans without some of the user's foods.
confirmed.evidence: lib/server/day-context.ts:241-258 (`foodsFor`). Callers: lib/server/day-context.ts:272 (`serverStoreFor`), lib/server/plan-ideas.ts:62, lib/server/compose-pool-ports.ts:28 and 46. Contrast with `userFoodRefIds` at day-context.ts:222-236.
votes:
confirmed: I read the code at lib/server/day-context.ts:241-258. `foodsFor` reads `user_foods` with `.eq(user_id)` only, with no `deleted_at` filter and no paging. `foodsFromSyncRows` (lib/store.ts:372) skips soft-deleted rows only after the read, so deleted ids still go into the `.in("user_food_id", ids)` list and into the `user_food_prefs` `.in("food_ref_id", refIds)` list. Both `.in()` calls are unbatched. The sibling `userFoodRefIds` (same file, lines 222-236) already fixes this with `deleted_at is null`, `fetchAllRows` and `fetchAllChunked`, and its comment names the 1,000-row cap, so the project treats this as a real hazard. I found no upstream guard and no ruling or audit in docs/decisions or docs/audit that accepts it. I did not reproduce the failure.

- **Callers:** `foodsFor` runs on every `serverStoreFor` call (which is the coach turn), in plan-ideas.ts:62, and in compose-pool-ports.ts:28 and 46.
- **Truncation:** past 1,000 rows the read silently drops foods. That is certain, and the only unproven part is how many foods an account must hold first.
- **URL length:** 36-character UUIDs in a GET query string give roughly 12 KB at about 300 ids. That is near typical gateway limits, but I did not confirm the actual PostgREST/Kong limit, so a 4xx from a "few hundred" foods is plausible rather than proven.

I rate it medium. The defect is real, but it only bites accounts with a very large food list.

confirmed: Confirmed by reading the code. I did not run a repro, so the exact URL-limit threshold is not measured. In lib/server/day-context.ts, foodsFor (lines 241-258) does `user_foods.select(...).eq("user_id")` with no `deleted_at` filter, no `.order()` and no paging. The API row cap is 1000 (paged-read.ts PAGE_SIZE), so a plain select silently truncates there. Soft-deleted rows count toward that cap. The cap can therefore push live foods out of the result. foodsFromSyncRows (lib/store.ts:~366) drops deleted rows only after they have been fetched, which confirms they are read and not filtered in SQL. The same function then runs `food_refs.in("user_food_id", ids)` with every id in one query string. It also runs `user_food_prefs.in("food_ref_id", refIds)` unbatched. Each uuid adds about 37 characters to the URL, so a few hundred ids give a URL of 10 KB or more. Those unbatched queries therefore risk a 4xx/414 failure, and they exceed the gateway budget that paged-read.ts sets for `.in()` lists (IN_CHUNK_SIZE of 150). The sibling userFoodRefIds (lines 222-236) already fixes this with `.is("deleted_at", null)`, fetchAllRows and fetchAllChunked, so foodsFor is the missed one. It is on the path of every coach turn (serverStoreFor), plan-ideas and compose pool. The impact is a failed coach or chip request, or a plan built without some of the user's foods. Medium severity fits: it needs hundreds of foods, but it fails at a scale that active accounts will reach.

confirmed.title: Authenticated users can write target_profiles directly, bypassing every server-side safety floor and pace hold
confirmed.defect: target_profiles is a pattern-1 owner table. Its policy target_profiles_rw is FOR ALL and the table is granted select, insert, update and delete to authenticated. Migration 20261006090100 tightened expenditure_estimates and target_proposals but states that target_profiles 'keeps its _rw policy'. No later migration revokes the DML grant or adds a guard trigger. confirmed.title: Meal cards keep their draft state across date switches: ingredient edits and the preview carry onto another day, and Save writes them to that day

Tuesday's Meal 1 card still shows Monday's edited ingredient list and the preview kcal, because `shown = dirty ? working : components`. Tapping 'Save ingredients' calls `saveSlotEdit` with `viewedDate = Tuesday`. That writes Monday's component list as Tuesday's item override, so the wrong foods and calories land on Tuesday and Tuesday's own plan is lost. Even without Save, the card shows the wrong calories for the new date.
confirmed.evidence: lib/today-timeline.ts:43,47 (`key: \`slot-${slot.slot}\``). app/page.tsx:1047,1074 (`<SlotCardEnter key={item.key} …>`; only DayTypeToggle is keyed by `viewedDate`, at :922). components/SlotCardDetail.tsx:73-110 (`useState(components)`, `shown = dirty ? working : components`) and :171-183 (`save` sends `working`). app/page.tsx:650-656 (`saveSlotEdit` uses `viewedDate`).
